I will willingly offer sacrifice to you. I will praise your name, Lord, because it is good.
For you saved me from every affliction, and my eye looked with satisfaction on my enemies.
For the director. With songs of praise. A song of understanding by David.
Listen to my prayer, God, and do not ignore my plea.
Pay attention to me and listen to me. I was distressed in my anxiety, and I was troubled
because of my enemy’s voice and the oppression of the sinner. For they brought lawlessness upon me and were furious with me.
My heart was troubled within me, and the terror of death fell upon me.
Fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me.
I said, “Who will give me wings like those of doves, so that I may fly away and rest?” Interlude.
Look, I fled far away and stayed in the wilderness.
I was waiting for the one who would save me from faintheartedness and the storm.
Drown them, Lord, and divide their tongues, for I saw lawlessness and strife in the city.
Day and night they will go around it on its walls. Lawlessness and hardship are within it.
Violence is within it, and usury and deceit have not left its streets.
For if an enemy had insulted me, I would have borne it. And if someone who hated me had spoken arrogantly against me, I would have hidden from him.
But you, the man close to my heart, my leader whom I know,
the one who used to share meals with me—we used to walk together in the house of God.
May death come upon them. Let them go down alive to the underworld, for wickedness is in their dwellings, in its midst.
But I cried out to God, and the Lord heard me.
I will speak in the evening, in the morning, and at noon. I will tell, and he will hear my voice.
And he will redeem my soul in peace from those who draw near me, for there were many with me.
God will hear and humble them, he who exists from before the ages. Interlude. For they do not change, and they have not feared God.
He stretched out his hand in repayment; he profaned his covenant.
They were divided by the anger of his face, and his heart drew near. His words were softer than oil, yet they were like arrows.
Cast your concern upon the Lord, and he will sustain you. He will never allow the righteous person to be shaken.
But you, God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction. Bloodthirsty and deceitful people will not reach half their days. But I will trust in you, Lord.
For the director. For the people who went far away from the holy ones. What David wrote on the pillar when the Philistines seized him in Gath.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for a man has trampled me; they have oppressed me in battle all day long.
My enemies have trampled on me all day long, for many fight against me for many days.
I will not be afraid; I trust in you.
I will honor my words in my God all day long. I have trusted in God; I will not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
They have detested my words all day long; all their thoughts are directed against me for evil.
They will gather and hide themselves. They will watch my heel, just as they have waited for my life.
Will you save them for nothing? God, you will bring down the nations in your anger.
I have told you my deeds. You have placed my tears before you, according to your promise as well.
My enemies will turn back on the day when I cry out to you. Look, I have learned that you are my God.
I will praise my God with my words. I will praise my God with my words.
I have put my hope in God; I will not be afraid. What can a human being do to me?
God, the vows are within me, and I will fulfill them. I will praise you.
For you have saved my soul from death and my feet from slipping, so that I may please God in his presence, in the light of the living.
For the end. Do not destroy. A pillar inscription of David, when he fled from Saul into the cave.
Have mercy on me, God, have mercy on me, for my soul has trusted in you. I will trust under the shadow of your wings until my lawlessness passes.
I will cry out to God Most High, the God who has done good to me.
The Lord sent from heaven and saved me. He exposed those who trample on me to reproach. Musical pause. God sent his mercy and his truth.
He saved my soul. I lay down troubled among lion cubs. The teeth of human beings are weapons and arrows, and their tongue is a sharp sword.
Exalt yourself, God, above the heavens, and let your glory be over all the earth.
They prepared a trap for my feet and bowed down my soul. They dug a pit before me and fell into it. Musical pause.
God, my heart is ready; my heart is ready. I will sing and make music to you.
Awake, my glory! Awake, harp and lyre! I will rise early.
I will give thanks to you, Lord, among the peoples. I will make music to you.
For your mercy has risen to the heavens, and your truth to the clouds.
Exalt yourself above the heavens, God, and let your glory be over all the earth.
For the end. Do not destroy. The psalm of David that he wrote on the pillar.
If you truly speak righteousness, judge uprightly, you children of humanity.
For indeed, you work lawless deeds in your heart on the earth; your hands weave acts of injustice.
Sinners have been estranged from the womb; they have gone astray from the belly, speaking lies.
Their venom is like a snake’s, like a deaf snake that closes its ears.
It does not listen to the voice of those who call to it, or to a charm performed by a skilled person.
God will shatter their teeth in their mouths; the Lord has broken the lions’ jaws.
He has scattered them like flowing water. He will draw his bow until they grow weak.
They will dissolve like melted wax. Fire fell upon them, and they did not see the sun.
Before they recognize their buckthorn thorns, he will swallow you up in anger like the living.
The righteous person will rejoice when he sees the punishment of the ungodly. He will wash his hands in the sinner’s blood.
And a person will say, “Then the righteous have a reward; then there is a God who judges them on earth.”
For the end. Do not destroy. What he wrote on the pillar, for David, when Saul sent men to watch his house to kill him.
God, save me from my enemies; deliver me from those who rise up against me.
Rescue me from those who practice lawlessness, and save me from bloodthirsty people.
For look, they have laid an ambush for my life; powerful people have come against me. Lord, it is not because of my lawlessness or my sin.
I ran without wrongdoing and kept a straight course. Rise up, come to meet me, and see.
You, Lord, God of hosts, God of Israel, give your attention to punishing all the nations. Do not have mercy on anyone who practices lawlessness. Pause.
They will return in the evening, be hungry like their dogs, and go around the city.
Look, they will speak with their mouths, with a sword on their lips, saying, “Who has heard?”
You, Lord, will laugh at them. You will mock every nation.
I will guard my strength before you, because you are my God, the one who takes me into your protection.
My God’s mercy will go before me. God will let me look my fill at my enemies.
Do not kill them, lest they forget your name. Scatter them by your power and bring them down, Lord, my protector.
The sin of their mouths is the speech of their lips. Let them be caught in their pride. They will proclaim their end because of their cursing and their lying.
And the wrath of destruction, so that they will no longer exist. And they will know that the God of Jacob rules over the ends of the earth. Pause.
They will return in the evening, be hungry like their dogs, and go around the city.
They will scatter in search of food, and if they are not satisfied, they will grumble.
But I will sing of your power and rejoice in your mercy in the morning, because you have become the one who takes me into your protection, and a refuge on the day of my distress.
You are my helper. I will sing praises to you, because you are God, the one who takes me into your protection, my God, my mercy.
For the end. For those who will change. Again, David’s inscription on a pillar, for succession.
When he burned Mesopotamia of Syria and Syria of Zobah, and Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand in Edom in the Valley of Salt.
God, you have rejected us and scattered us. You were angry, yet you have again had mercy on us.
You shook the earth and disturbed it. Heal all its cracks, for it has been shaken.
You showed your people hard things; you made us drink wine of anguish.
You gave a sign to those who fear you, so that they might flee from the bow.
So that your beloved ones may be rescued, save me with your right hand and hear me. Pause.
God spoke in his sanctuary: “I will rejoice. I will divide Shechem and measure out the valley of tents.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim is the strength of my head. Judah is my king.
Moab is the basin of my hope. I will stretch out my sandal over Edom, and the Philistines will submit to me.”
Who will bring me into the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
Is it not you, God, who rejected us? Yet you do not go out with our armies, God.
Lord, give us help in our troubles, for human deliverance is useless.
With our God we will act mightily, and he will trample those who oppress us.
For the end. With praises. Of David.
God, hear my plea; pay attention to my prayer.
From the end of the earth I cried out to you when my heart was in anguish. You lifted me up onto a rock and led me.
For you became my hope, a strong tower against the enemy.
I will dwell in your dwelling place forever. I will take shelter in the shadow of your wings. Pause.
For you, God, heard my prayer. You gave your inheritance to those who fear your name.
Day by day he will add to the years of his king, until the day of one generation after another.
He will remain forever before God. His mercy and his truth—who will seek them?
Thus I will sing praise to your name, God, forever and ever, fulfilling my vows day by day.
For the end. Concerning Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
Will my soul not submit to God? For my salvation comes from him.
For he is God, my Savior, the one who receives me to himself. I will not be greatly shaken.
How long will you rise up against a person, all of you committing murder, like a leaning wall and a fence that has been pushed over?
But they plotted to set aside my honor. They rushed together into falsehood. They blessed with their mouths while cursing in their hearts. Pause.
But, my soul, submit to the Lord, for my patient hope comes from him.
For he is God, my Savior, the one who receives me; I will not be shaken.
My salvation rests with my God, and God is my glory. God is my help and my hope.
Trust in him, every assembly of people. Pour out your hearts before him. Musical pause. God is our helper.
Yet human beings are empty; human beings are lies. On dishonest scales, they are all alike, nothing but emptiness.
Do not trust in injustice, and do not set your hearts on robbery. If wealth comes, do not set your hearts on it.
God has spoken once; I have heard these things twice: my strength belongs to God.
And mercy belongs to you, Lord, for you will repay each person according to their deeds.
The psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Idumea.
God, my God, I seek you early. My soul has thirsted for you, and my flesh has wasted away in a desert land, impassable and without water.
This is how I appeared to you in the sanctuary, to see your power and your glory.
For your mercy is better than life. My lips will praise you.
This is how I will praise you throughout my life, and I will lift up my hands in your name.
My soul is satisfied with fat and marrow; joyful lips will praise your name.
When I remember you on my bed, I meditate on you in the early morning.
For you have been my helper, and I will rejoice in the shadow of your wings.
My soul has clung to you; your right hand has received me.
But they have sought my soul to destroy it. They will go down into the depths of the earth.
They will be handed over to the power of the sword; they will become food for foxes.
But the king will rejoice in God. Everyone who swears by him will receive honor, for the mouths of those who speak unjustly have been shut.
For the end. A psalm of David.
My God, hear my voice as I plead with you. Rescue my soul from fear of the enemy.
You have sheltered me from the gathering of evildoers, from the crowd that practices lawlessness.
They have sharpened their tongues like swords and drawn their bow for a bitter deed.
They shoot arrows in secret at the holy one. They will shoot at him suddenly and will not be afraid.
They have strengthened themselves in an evil plan. They have spoken of hiding traps; they have said, “Who will see us?”
They have searched out lawless deeds, and [?] while they search, God will examine them. A person will advance with a hidden heart.
And the Lord my God will recognize him and be exalted. Their wounds have become little children's arrows.
And their tongues grew weak within them; all who saw them were shaken.
And everyone was afraid. They spoke of God's works and understood what he had made.
The righteous person will rejoice in the Lord and trust in him, and everyone who is upright in heart will receive honor.
For the end. A psalm of song, belonging to David, of Jeremiah and Ezekiel, concerning the place of exile, as they were coming out.
Praise is fitting for you, God, in Zion, and they will fulfill their vows to you in Jerusalem.
Listen to our prayer; everyone is coming before you.
The words of the lawless have prevailed over us, and you are the one who will forgive our sins.

Blessed is the one you have chosen and welcomed to yourself. He will live in your courts. We will be satisfied with the good things of your house. Your temple is holy; it is a wonder in righteousness.
Listen to us, God our Savior, the hope of all the ends of the earth,
and of those on the distant sea, the one who establishes the mountains by his strength, who is clothed with power,
who stirs up the vast sea and the sound of its waves.
The nations will be shaken, and those who live at the ends of the earth will be afraid because of your signs. You will bring joy to the paths of morning and evening.
You visited the earth and drenched it; you made it abundantly rich. God's river was filled with water. You prepared their food, for this is their preparation.
Let its furrows be drenched; multiply its crops. It will rejoice in the drops of water as it grows.
You will bless the crown of the year with your goodness, and the fields will flourish.
The mountains of the wilderness will sprout, and the hills will clothe themselves with rejoicing.
The valleys will increase their grain, and the sheepfolds have flourished. They will shout aloud; indeed, they will give praise.
For the end. A psalm of song of the resurrection. Shout joyfully to God, all the earth.
Sing to his name; give glory to his praise.
Say to God, "Your works are fearsome! Because of your great power, your enemies will lie to you."
Let all the earth worship you and sing to you. Let them sing to your name, Most High. Musical interlude.
Come, my children, and see God's works. He is more fearsome in his plans than human beings.
He turns the sea into dry land. They will walk through the river on foot. There we will rejoice in him.
He rules forever by his power; his eyes watch over the nations. Do not let the rebellious exalt themselves among themselves. Musical interlude.
Nations, praise our God, and make the sound of his praise heard.
He who kept my soul alive did not let our feet slip.
For you tested us, God; you refined us as silver is refined.
You brought us into the snare; you placed distress before us.
You made people ride over our heads. We passed through fire and water, and you brought me out to a place of rest.
I will enter your house with burnt offerings.
I will fulfill my vows to you, which my lips uttered and my mouth spoke in my humiliation.
I will offer you fat burnt offerings. I will offer you cattle and goats, with the smoke of rams. Pause.
All who fear God, come and listen, and I will tell you what the Lord my God has done for my soul.
I cried out to him with my mouth, and I raised my voice with my tongue.
If I have seen injustice in my heart, do not let the Lord listen to me.
Therefore God listened to me; he paid attention to the sound of my plea.
Blessed is God, who has not turned my prayer away from himself or his mercy away from me.
For the end. With blessings. A psalm, a song.
God, have mercy on us and bless us. Let your face shine upon us. Pause.
So that we may know your way on earth and your salvation among all the nations.
Let the peoples praise you, God. God, let all the peoples praise you.
Let the nations be glad and rejoice, for you will judge the peoples fairly; you will guide the nations on earth. Pause.
Let the peoples praise you, God; let all the peoples praise you.
The earth has yielded its fruit. Our God, bless us.
Bless us, our God, and let all the ends of the earth fear you.
For the end. A psalm, a song of David.
Let God arise, and let his enemies scatter; let those who hate him flee from his presence.
Let them vanish as smoke vanishes. As wax melts before fire, so let sinners perish before the face of God.
Let the righteous be glad and rejoice in the presence of God; let them delight in joy.
Sing to God and sing praises to his name. Prepare the way for him who ascended over the regions of the sunset. The Lord is his name. They will be troubled in his presence.
The father of orphans and the judge of widows is God in his holy place.
God will make those of one mind dwell in a house. He is the one who brought out those bound in bronze fetters with strength, along with the rebellious who dwell in tombs.
O God, when you went out before your people, when you went out through the wilderness,
the earth shook, and the heavens rained before the God of Sinai, before the God of Israel.
You will shower rain of your choosing, O God, upon your inheritance. It grew weak, but you restored it.
Your living creatures will dwell in it. In your goodness you made provision for the poor.
The Lord will give a message to those who proclaim good news with great power.
The king of the beloved one's armies, and the master of the house, to divide the spoils.
If you lie down among the allotted portions, a dove's wings are covered with silver, and the area around her neck with greenish gold. Pause.
When the one in heaven scatters kings over it, it will become white in Zalmon.
The mountain of God, the fertile mountain, the high mountain, the solid mountain, the fertile mountain.
Why do you think of the proud mountains? This is the mountain where God wished to dwell. Indeed, the Lord will dwell in it forever.
God's chariots number twenty thousand, thousands flourishing. The Lord is among them in Sinai, his holy place.
He ascended on high; he took captives captive; he gave gifts to people, even though they were unbelieving, in order to dwell.
Lord God, you are blessed forever and ever. The Lord, the God of our salvation, will make things go well for us. Pause.
Our God is the God of deliverance, and escape from death belongs to the Lord.
But God will crush the heads of their enemies, and the crowns of the heads of those who walk in their sins.
The Lord said, as he turned back from Bashan, "I will return from the depths of the sea,
so that your foot may be dipped in blood, and the tongues of your dogs will lick from the enemies who oppose him."
They saw your processions, O God, the processions of my God, the king who is in the holy place.
The rulers went ahead, close to the singers, among the young women playing tambourines.
Bless God in the assemblies, the Lord, from the springs of Israel.
There is Benjamin, the youngest, in ecstasy; the rulers of Judah with their leaders; the rulers of Zebulun; the rulers of Naphtali.
O God, command your power. O God, strengthen what you have prepared for us.
Kings will bring you gifts to your temple in Jerusalem.

O God, rebuke the wild beasts of the wooded place and the reed bed, the gathering of bulls among the calves of the people, so as not to turn back those who have been tested with silver. He scattered the nations that desire war.
Envoys are coming from Egypt. The Ethiopians will be the first to extend their hands to God.
Kings of the earth, bless God; sing praises to the Lord. Pause.
Sing to God, who ascended above the heaven of heaven in the east. Look, there is a voice of blessing in his voice.
Give glory to God. His greatness is over Israel, and his power is in the clouds.
God is wonderful among his holy ones. The God of Israel is the one who will give strength and firmness to his people. Blessed is God.
For the end. For those who will change. The psalm of David.
God, save me, for waters have reached my soul.
I sank into the mud of the deep, and there is no strength. I came into the depths of the sea, and a storm submerged me.
I grew weary from crying out. My throat dried up. My eyes failed as I waited for God.
Those who hate me without cause have become more numerous than the hairs of my head. My enemies, who persecute me unjustly, have grown strong. They demanded things that I had not stolen.
God, you know my foolishness, and my sins have not been hidden from you.
Do not let those who wait for you be ashamed because of me, Lord of hosts. Do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me, Lord, God of Israel, God of hosts.
For your sake I have borne reproach; shame has covered my face.
I became a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother's children.
For zeal for your house consumed me, and the insults of those who insult you fell upon me.
I humbled my soul with fasting, and it became a reproach to me.
I put sackcloth on myself, and I became a byword to them.
Those who sit at the gates spoke against me, and those who drink wine sang about me.
But I prayed to you in my soul, Lord. It is the time of your favor. God, in the abundance of your mercy, listen to my salvation in truth.
Save me from the mud, so that I do not sink in it. May I be saved from those who hate me and from the depths of the waters.
Do not let a flood of water submerge me. Do not let the deep swallow me. Do not let a pit close its mouth over me.
Hear me, Lord, for your mercy is good. Look upon me according to the abundance of your compassion.
Do not turn your face away from your servant, for I am in distress. Hear me quickly.
Pay attention to my soul and redeem it. Rescue me because of my enemies.
For you know my reproach, my shame, and my disgrace. All who afflict me are before you.
My heart expected reproach and misery. I looked for someone who would grieve with me, but I found none, and for someone who would comfort me, but I found no one.
They put gall in my food, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let their table become a snare and a trap before them, a repayment and a stumbling block.
Let their eyes grow dark so that they cannot see, and bend their backs continually.
Pour out your wrath on them, and let your fierce anger overtake them.
Let their dwelling become deserted, and let no one live in their dwellings.
For they pursued the one you struck, and they added to the pain of his flesh.
Add lawlessness to their lawlessness, and do not let them enter into your righteousness.
Let them be erased from the book of the living, and do not let them be recorded with the righteous.
I am poor and suffering. The salvation that comes from your presence, God, has taken me in.
I will praise the name of God with a song; I will exalt him with praise.
This will please God more than a young calf growing horns and hooves.
Let the poor see and rejoice. Seek God, and your soul will live.
For the Lord has listened to the poor, and he has not despised those bound in bronze fetters.
Let the heavens and the earth praise the Lord, the sea and everything in it.
For God will save Zion, and they will build the cities of Judea. They will settle there and inherit it.
The descendants of his servants will possess it, and those who love his name will live in it.
For the end. Of David. For remembrance, that the Lord may give me life.
Lord God, give your attention to helping me.
Let those who seek my life be ashamed and disgraced. Let those who intend evil against me turn back and be ashamed.
Let those who say to me, “Well done! Well done!” turn back immediately and be ashamed.
Let everyone who seeks you rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your salvation always say, “May God be exalted!”
But I am poor and needy. Lord, help me. You are my helper and my protector. Lord, do not delay.
For the end. A psalm of David. God, God, I have trusted in you. Never let me be put to shame.
Save me in your righteousness and rescue me. Turn your ear toward me and save me.
Be a protecting God to me and a secure place to save me, for you are my strength and my refuge.
My God, save me from the hand of the sinner, from the hand of the lawless and the ungodly.
For you, Lord, are the one I wait for. Lord, you are my hope from my youth.
I have relied on you since I was in the womb. You brought me out of my mother's womb. I remember you at all times.
I have become like a sign to many. You are my helper and my strength. You are my Savior, Lord.
My mouth has been filled with praise, so that all day long I may praise the glory of your greatness.
Do not cast me away in old age. When my soul grows weak, do not abandon me.
For my enemies have spoken evil against me, and those who watch my life have plotted against my life, saying together:
"God has abandoned him. Pursue him and catch him, for there is no one to rescue him."
My God, do not stay far away from me. My God, attend to helping me.
Let those who slander my soul be ashamed and perish. Let those who seek to harm me be clothed in shame and disgrace.
But I will always trust in you, Lord my God, and I will add to your praise.
My mouth will speak of your righteousness and your salvation all day long, for I have not known commerce.
I come in your strength, Lord God. I will remember your righteousness, yours alone.
God, you have taught me from my youth, and to this day I will tell of your wonders.
Even in my old age and advanced years, God, do not abandon me until I proclaim your arm’s strength to the whole coming generation.
Your strength and your righteousness, God, reach to the heights—the great things you have done. God, who will seek you?
The troubles you have shown me many times, and the evils—you turned back and brought me to life; you brought me up from the depths of the earth.
You increased your greatness over me, and you turned back and comforted me.
For I too, Lord my God, will proclaim your truth among the peoples. I will sing to you with a lyre, Holy One of Israel.
My lips will rejoice when I sing to you, and so will my soul, which you redeemed from the hands of enemies.
My tongue too will speak of your righteousness all day long, when those who seek to harm me are ashamed and disgraced.
For Solomon. God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king's son,
to judge your people with uprightness and your poor with justice.
Let the mountains receive peace for your people, and the hills righteousness.
He will judge the poor among the people, save the children of the needy, and humble the oppressor.
And let him endure with the sun and before the moon, for generation after generation.
He comes down like rain upon a fleece, and like rain falling upon the earth.
Let righteousness flourish in his days, and abundant peace, until the moon is taken away.
And let him rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the inhabited world.
The Ethiopians will bow down before him, and his enemies will lick the earth.
The kings of Tarshish and the islands will bring him gifts. The kings of Arabia and Sheba will bring him gifts.
And let all kings bow down to him. All nations will serve him.
For he rescued the poor from the hand of the violent, and the needy who had no helper.
He will spare the poor and needy and save the lives of the needy.
He will redeem their lives from usury and violence; their name is honored in his sight.
He will live, and they will give him gold from Arabia. They will pray for him at all times and bless him all day long.
He will be a support for the earth upon the mountains. His fruit will rise above Lebanon, and they will flourish in the city like the grass of the earth.
His name will be blessed forever. His name exists before the sun. All the tribes of the earth will receive blessing through him; all the nations will call him blessed.
Blessed is the Lord God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonderful things.
And blessed is his glorious name forever and forever and ever. The whole earth will be filled with his glory. May it be so! May it be so!
The blessings of David, the son of Jesse, have ended. The psalm of Asaph. God is good to Israel, to those who are upright in heart.
But as for me, my feet almost slipped; my steps almost gave way.
For I envied the lawless when I saw the peace of sinners.
For there is no rest in their death, and they are firm under their affliction.
They do not share in human hardship, nor are they afflicted along with other people.
Because of this, their pride gave them strength; they clothed themselves in their violence and wickedness.
Their violence comes out as though from their fat; they came out plotting in their hearts.
They plotted and spoke wickedly; they spoke of violence from on high.
They raised their mouths up to heaven, and their tongues went out over the earth.
Because of this, my people will return here, and days of fullness will be found for them.
They said, “How did God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Look, these are the sinners who prosper; they have held on to their wealth forever.
And I said, “Surely I purified my heart in vain; I washed my hands among the holy.”
I was being whipped all day long, and my rebuke came in the morning.
If I said, “I will speak this way,” look, I have made an agreement with the generation of your children.
I thought about knowing the Lord; this was difficult in my sight,
until I entered the holy places of God to understand their end.
Yet you positioned them because of their deceit; you cast them down when they exalted themselves.
How suddenly they became desolate! They failed and perished because of their lawlessness.
Like the dream of those who wake up, Lord, you will despise their image in your city.
For my heart rejoiced, and my kidneys were changed.
But I am foolish and did not understand. I became like the animals before you.
But I am with you at all times. You took hold of my right hand.
You guided me with your counsel and received me to yourself with glory.
For what do I have in heaven? And what have I wanted from you on earth?
My heart and my flesh failed. God is the God of my heart and my portion forever.
For look, those who are far from you will perish. You have wiped out everyone who acts wickedly before you.
But it is good for me to draw near to God, to place my hope in the Lord, to tell of all your promises in the gates of the daughter of Zion.
The instruction of Asaph. Why, God, have you abandoned us forever? Your anger has raged against the sheep of your flock.
Remember your congregation, which you acquired for yourself from the beginning. You redeemed the tribe of your inheritance, this Mount Zion in which you settled.
Raise your hands against their arrogance forever, against the evils the enemy committed in your holy places.
Those who hate you boasted in the midst of your festival. They set up their signs as signs, and they did not understand.
You will destroy their way of entering [?] above. They chopped down its doors with axes, like trees in the countryside.
They demolished it with an axe and a hammer together.
They burned your sanctuary with fire. They tore down the dwelling place of your name.
Their whole clan said together in their hearts, “Come, let us remove God's festivals from the earth.”
We have not seen their signs. There is no prophet, and then he will know for us.
How long, God, will the enemy taunt? Will your opponent revile your name forever?
Why have you drawn back your hand forever, and your right hand into your bosom?
Our God is our king from eternity. He worked his salvation in the midst of the earth.
You made the sea firm by your power. You crushed the heads of the dragons upon the water.
You crushed the heads of the dragon. You gave it as food to the peoples of the Ethiopians.
You are the one who split open springs and rushing waters. You are the one who made the mighty rivers dry up.
The day is yours, and the night is yours. You are the one who prepared the light and the sun.
You established all the boundaries of the earth; you formed summer and spring.
Remember this creation of yours: the enemy has mocked the Lord, and a foolish people has reviled his name.
Do not give a soul that acknowledges you to the wild beasts. Do not forget the souls of the poor forever.
Look upon your covenant, for the houses of the violent people of the earth are filled with lawlessness.
Do not let the humbled person turn back in shame. The poor and the needy will bless your name.
Rise up, God, and judge my case. Remember the insults that the foolish person directs against you all day long.
Do not forget the voice of your servants. The arrogance of those who hate you has risen to you continually.
For the end. “Do not destroy.” A psalm, a song of Asaph.
God, we will give thanks to you; we will give thanks to you and call on your name.
I will tell of your wonders. When I find the appointed time, Lord, I will judge justly.
The earth dissolved, along with everyone living on it. I made its pillars firm. Pause.
I said to the lawless, “Do not act lawlessly,” and to sinners, “Do not raise your horn.”
Do not raise your horn toward heaven. Do not speak against God with violence.
For he is not despised in the west, nor from the desert mountains.
For God is a judge: he humbles one and raises another.
For there is a cup in the Lord’s hand, filled to the brim with unmixed wine. He pours from this into that, but its dregs have not been emptied out. All the sinners of the earth will drink.
But I will rejoice forever. I will sing praises to the God of Jacob. I will proclaim them forever.
I will break all the horns of sinners, but the horns of the righteous will be raised.
For the end, with praises. A psalm, a song of Asaph.
God is known in Judea; his name is great in Israel.
His dwelling place came to be in peace, and his home is in Zion.
For there he shattered the strength of the bows, the weapon, the sword, and warfare. Pause.
You shine wonderfully.
All the foolish were troubled in their hearts, from the everlasting mountains. They forgot in their forgetfulness. None of the wealthy men found anything in their hands.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, all those mounted on horses became drowsy.
You are terrifying. Who can stand against you? Your anger has existed from eternity.
You, Lord, made judgment heard from heaven. The earth was afraid and became still,
when God rose up for judgment, to save all the humble people of the earth. Pause.
For human thought will acknowledge you, and the remainder of that thought will celebrate a festival for you.
Make vows and fulfill them to the Lord our God. Everyone around him will bring him gifts.
He inspires fear and takes away the spirit of rulers; he inspires fear in all the kings of the earth.
For the director, according to Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph.
I cried aloud with my voice to the Lord, with my voice to God, and he paid attention to me.
I sought the Lord on the day of my distress, with my hands before you at night, and I was not deceived. My soul refused to be comforted.
I remembered God and rejoiced. I pondered, and my spirit grew faint. Pause.
My eyes were awake before the night watches. I was troubled and did not speak.
I thought about the days of old. I remembered the years of long ago and meditated on them.
I spoke with my heart at night, and I was troubled in my spirit.
Will the Lord reject us forever and no longer be pleased with us?
Or will he cut off his mercy completely, from generation to generation? Or will God forget to be compassionate?
Or will he withhold his compassion in his anger? Pause.
And I said, “Now I have begun. This is the change of the right hand of the Most High.”
I remembered the Lord’s deeds, for I will remember your wonders from the beginning.
I will meditate on all your deeds and ponder your thoughts.
Your way, God, comes forth in the sanctuary. Who is a great god like our God?
You alone are the God who works wonders. You revealed your power among the peoples.
You redeemed your people with your arm, the children of Jacob and Joseph. Pause.
The waters saw you, God; the waters saw you and were afraid. The depths were troubled at the mighty roar of the waters.
The clouds gave voice, and indeed your arrows will travel.
The sound of your thunder was in the wheel. Your lightning lit up the inhabited world. The earth moved and shook.
Your way is in the sea, and your paths are in mighty waters, and your footprints will not be known.
You led your people like sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
A psalm of instruction, by Asaph. Pay attention, my people, to my law. Incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in parables. I will speak riddles from long ago.
The things we have heard and understood, the things our ancestors told us,
they did not hide from their children, telling [?] the praises of the Lord, his mighty deeds, and the wonders he performed.
A testimony was established in Jacob, and he laid down a law in Israel, which he commanded our ancestors to make known to their children,
so that another generation would know—the children yet to be born—and they would rise and tell their children,
so that they would put their hope in God, not forget God's deeds, and seek his commandments,
so that they would not become like their ancestors, a crooked and rebellious generation, a generation that did not set its heart right and whose spirit was not faithful to God.
The children of Ephraim, drawing bows and shooting arrows, turned back on the day of battle.
They did not keep God's covenant and did not want to walk according to his law.
They forgot his good deeds, which he had shown their ancestors before their eyes,
the wonders he performed in the land of Egypt, in the plain of Zoan.
He split the sea and brought them out; he made the waters stand like a wineskin.
He led them with a cloud by day and with the light of fire throughout the night.
He split a rock in the wilderness and gave them drink as abundant as the deep.
He brought water out of a rock and made water flow down like rivers.
They continued to sin against him and rebelled against the Most High in a waterless place.
They tested God in their hearts by asking for food for themselves.
They spoke against God, saying, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?”
Because he struck a rock, waters poured out and streams flowed. Can he also give us bread or prepare a table for his people?
Because of this, the Lord heard and became angry. A fire blazed in Jacob, and wrath came upon Israel,
because they did not believe in God or put their hope in his salvation.
They commanded the clouds above them, and he opened the doors of heaven.
He rained manna on them to eat and gave them the bread of heaven.
Human beings ate the bread of angels. He sent them food until they were satisfied.
He stirred up the south wind from heaven and brought the west wind by his power.
He rained meat on them like dust, and flying birds like the sand of the sea.
They fell in the middle of their camp and around their dwelling place.
They ate and were completely satisfied; he brought them what they wanted.
They had not satisfied their craving; the food was still in their mouths.
God’s wrath came down upon them. He killed the strongest of them and brought down Israel’s chosen men.
Despite all this, they sinned again and did not believe in his wonders.
Their days ended in futility, and their years in haste.
When he killed some of them, they sought him. They turned back and hurried to God.
They remembered that God was their helper and that God Most High was their redeemer.
They loved him with their mouths, but lied to him with their tongues.
Their hearts were not upright toward him, nor were they faithful to his covenant.
But he is compassionate. He will forgive their sins and not destroy them. He will repeatedly turn away his anger and will not stir up all his wrath.
He remembered that they were flesh, a breath that goes away and does not return.
Many times they angered him in the wilderness and grieved him in a place where there was no water.
Again they turned back and tested God, and they grieved the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember his power or the day when he rescued them from the hands of those who oppressed them.
How he performed his signs in Egypt and his wonders in the plain of Zoan.
He turned their rivers into blood, and the water of their springs, so that they could not drink.
He sent dogflies upon them, which devoured them, and frogs, which destroyed them.
He gave their crops to caterpillars and the fruits of their labor to locusts.
He killed their grapevines with hail and their sycamore trees with frost.
He gave their livestock over to hail and their possessions to fire.
He sent down upon them the fury of his anger: anger, wrath, and distress, sent through evil angels.
They made a way for his wrath. He did not spare their lives from death, and he handed their livestock over to be killed.
He struck every firstborn of the Egyptians, the firstfruits of their labor in the dwellings of Ham.
He led his people out like sheep and brought them through the wilderness like a flock.
He led them with hope, and they did not grow weak. The sea covered their enemies.
He brought them into his holy mountain, this mountain that his right hand acquired for itself.
He drove out nations before them and allotted their inheritance to them with a measuring cord. He gave their dwelling places to the tribes of Israel to live in.
Yet again they tested and provoked God Most High and did not keep his decrees.
They turned away and became rebellious like their ancestors. They turned into a crooked bow.
They provoked him with their altars and made him jealous with their handmade images.
God heard and became angry, and he utterly rejected Israel.
He abandoned the dwelling at Shiloh, his place where he had lived among people.
He gave their strength into captivity and their splendor into the enemy's hand.
He delivered his people to the sword and became angry with his inheritance.
Fire consumed their young men, and their virgins did not mourn.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows did not weep.
The Lord rose like someone waking from sleep, like a warrior who had stumbled under the influence of wine.
He struck his enemies from behind; he gave them everlasting disgrace.
He abandoned the dwelling of Joseph and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.
He built his holy place like a unicorn and established its foundation on the earth forever.
He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds.
He took him from following the ewes with young to shepherd Jacob his people and Israel his inheritance.
He shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.
A psalm of Asaph. God, nations have entered your inheritance. They have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem like a watch post.
They gave the dead bodies of your servants as food to the birds of the sky, and the flesh of your holy ones to the wild animals of the earth.
They poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
We have become a disgrace to our neighbors, an object of mockery and laughter to those around us.
How long, Lord? Will you be angry forever? Will your fire blaze like a fire?
Pour out your anger on the nations that have not known you and on the kingdoms that have not called on your name.
For they have devoured Jacob and made his dwelling place a wilderness.
Do not remember our former sins. Let your mercies reach us quickly, for we have become very poor.
Help us, God our Savior, for the glory of your name. Lord, save us and forgive our lawless deeds for your name's sake.
Do not let them say among the nations, “Where is their God?” Let vengeance for the blood of your servants that they have poured out be made known among the nations before our eyes.
Let the groaning of those bound in bronze shackles come before you. Save the children of those who have been killed, according to the greatness of your arm.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their laps for the insult with which they have insulted you, Lord.
For we are your people and the sheep of your pasture. We will give thanks to you forever; we will proclaim your praises from generation to generation.
For the end. Concerning those who will change. A testimony of Asaph. A psalm concerning the Assyrian.
Shepherd of Israel, listen, you who lead Joseph like sheep. You who sit enthroned upon the cherubim, reveal yourself.
Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up your power and come to save us.
God, restore us. Reveal your face, and we will be saved.
Lord, God of hosts, how long will you be angry at the prayer of your servants?
You will feed us bread of tears and give us tears to drink in measure.
You have made us an object of contention among our neighbors, and our enemies have mocked us.
God of hosts, restore us and reveal your face to us, so that we may be saved. Musical pause.
You brought a grapevine out of Egypt; you drove out nations and planted it.
You cleared the way before it; you planted its roots, and the land was filled.
Its shade covered the mountains, and its branches covered the cedars of God.
It spread its branches as far as the sea, and its shoots as far as the river.
Why have you torn down its fence, so that everyone passing along the road plucks its fruit?
A boar from the field has ruined it, and a wild donkey has grazed on it.
Restore us, then, God of hosts. Look down from heaven, see, and tend this vine.
Restore what your right hand planted, and the son of man whom you made strong for yourself.
It is burned with fire and dug up. They will perish at the rebuke of your face.
Let your hand be upon the man of your right hand, and upon the son of man whom you made strong for yourself.
Then we will not turn away from you. You will give us life, and we will call upon your name.
Lord, God of hosts, restore us and reveal your face to us, so that we may be saved.
For the end. Concerning the winepresses. A psalm of Asaph, for the fifth day of the week.
Rejoice in God, our helper; shout for joy to the God of Jacob.
Take up a psalm and bring a tambourine, a sweet-sounding harp and a lyre.
Blow trumpets at the new moon, on the announced day of our festival.
For this is a command for Israel and a decree of the God of Jacob.
He established it as a testimony for Joseph when he came out of the land of Egypt. He heard a language he did not know.
He turned his shoulder away from a burden; his hands served with a basket.
You cried out to me in distress, and I rescued you. I heard you in the hidden place of thunder. I tested you at the water of dispute. Pause.
Listen, my people, and I will speak to you. Israel, I will testify to you, if you will listen to me.
There shall be no new god among you, nor shall you worship a foreign god.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. Open your mouth, and I will fill it.
My people did not listen to my voice; Israel paid no attention to me.
I sent them away according to the desires of their hearts; they will walk in their own ways.
If only my people had listened to me, if only Israel had walked in my ways,
I would have humbled their enemies in no time, and I would have brought my hands against those who oppress them.
The Lord’s enemies lied to him, and their time will last forever.
He fed them with the finest wheat and satisfied them with honey from a rock.
A psalm of Asaph. God stood in the assembly of the gods, and in their midst he will judge the gods.
How long will you judge unjustly and show favoritism to sinners? Pause.
Give justice to the orphan and the poor; vindicate the lowly and the needy.
Save the needy and the poor; rescue them from the hand of sinners.
They did not know or understand; they walk in darkness. The foundations of the earth will be shaken.
I said, “You are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.”
Look, you will die like human beings, and you will fall like one of the rulers.
Rise, God, and judge the earth, for you are the one who will wipe out all the nations.
A song. A psalm of Asaph.
God, Lord, who will seek you? Do not remain silent, God, and do not hold back.
For look, your enemies have cried out, and those who hate you have raised their heads.
They devised an evil plan against your people and plotted against your holy ones.
They said, “Come, let us wipe them out from among the nations, so that the name of Israel will no longer exist.”
Together they agreed on a single plan; they made a covenant against you:
the dwelling place of the Edomites and the Ishmaelites, Moab and those descended from Hagar.
Gebal, Ammon, Amalek, the Philistines, and those who live in Tyre.
For Assyria too joined them; they gave support to the sons of Lot. Pause.
Do to them what you did to Midian and Sisera, and as you did to Jabin at the Kishon torrent.
They were destroyed in a place without water; they became like dung on the ground.
Make their rulers like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their rulers like Zebah and Zalmunna.
These are the ones who said, “Let us take God's holy place as our own possession.”
My God, make them like a wheel, like straw before the wind.
Like a fire that burns a forest, and like a flame burning mountains.
In this way, pursue them with your storm and terrify them with your anger.
Fill their faces with disgrace, and they will seek your name, Lord.
Let them be ashamed and troubled forever and ever; let them be humiliated and perish.
And let them know that your name is the Lord, that you alone are the Most High over the whole earth.
For the choirmaster. Concerning the winepresses. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
How lovely your dwelling places are, Lord of hosts!
My soul longed for your courts and grew faint for them, Lord. My heart and my flesh rejoiced in the living God.
For even a sparrow has found a home for itself, and a swallow a nest for herself, a place where she will lay her young:
Your altars, Lord of hosts, my King and my God.
Blessed are all who live in your house; they will praise you forever and ever. Pause. Blessed is the person whom you will receive to yourself, Lord.
He has set thoughts in his heart toward the valley of weeping, the place he established. For the lawgiver will give blessings.
They will go from strength to strength. The God of gods will appear in Zion.
Hear my prayer, Lord God of hosts; listen to me, God of Jacob. Pause.
Look, God, our protector, and look upon the face of your anointed one.
For one day in your courts is better than a thousand outside them. I have chosen rather to be cast aside in God's house than to live in the dwellings of sinners.
For the Lord God loves mercy and truth, and he will give grace and glory. The Lord will not deprive those who walk in innocence of good things.
Lord God of hosts, blessed is the person who puts his hope in you.
For the choirmaster. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
Lord, you have favored your land; you have brought Jacob back from captivity.
You have forgiven your people's lawlessness; you have covered all their sins. Musical interlude.
You have calmed all your wrath; you have turned away from your fierce anger.
Restore us, God of our salvation, and turn your anger away from us.
Will you be angry with us forever? Will you prolong your wrath from generation to generation?
God, you will turn back and revive us, and your people will rejoice in you.
Show us your mercy, Lord, and give us your salvation.
I will listen to what the Lord God will say within me, for he will speak peace to his people and to his holy ones, and to those who turn their hearts toward him.
Indeed, his salvation is near to those who fear him,
so that glory may dwell in our land. Mercy and truth have met one another; righteousness and peace have kissed one another.
Truth has sprouted from the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven.
For our God will also give goodness, and our land will yield its fruit.
Righteousness will walk before him, and he will set his footsteps on a path.
A prayer of David. Lord, incline your ear and listen to me, for I am poor and needy.
Guard my soul, for I am holy. God, save your servant who places his hope in you.
Have mercy on me, Lord, for I have cried out to you all day long.
Gladden the soul of your servant, for I have lifted my soul up to you, Lord.
For you, Lord, are good and gentle; your mercy is abundant toward everyone who calls out to you.
Lord, listen to my prayer and pay attention to the sound of my plea.
On the day of my distress, I cried out to you, for you listened to me.
There is no one like you among the gods, Lord, and there are no works like yours.
All the nations you have made will come and worship before you, Lord, and glorify your name.
For you are great and do wonders; you alone are the great God.
Guide me, Lord, in your way, and I will walk in your truth. Let my heart rejoice in fearing your name.
I will give thanks to you, Lord God, with all my heart, and I will glorify your name forever.
For your mercy toward me is great, and you have rescued my soul from the depths of the underworld. Pause.
God, lawless people have risen against me, and a gathering of violent people has sought my life. They have not kept you before their eyes.
For you, Lord God, are compassionate and merciful, patient, abundant in mercy, and faithful.
Look upon me and have mercy on me. Give strength to your servant and save the son of your servant girl.
Give me a sign of your goodness, and let those who hate me see it and be ashamed, because you, Lord, have helped me and comforted me.
A psalm, a song of the sons of Korah. His foundations are in the holy mountains.
The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwelling places of Jacob.
Glorious things have been spoken about you, city of God. Pause.
I will remember Rahab and Babylon among those who know me, Lord. Look, the Philistines, Tyre, and the people of Ethiopia—these were born there.
A person will say, “Zion is my mother,” and a person was born in her. He himself established her foundations forever.
The Lord Most High will speak in the register of the peoples and the rulers who were born in her.
For the dwelling place of all who rejoice is in you.
A song, a psalm of the sons of Korah. For the end, according to Mahalath, to be sung in response. An instruction of Heman the Israelite.
Lord, God of my salvation, I have cried out before you by day and by night.
Let my prayer come before you. Turn your ear, Lord, toward my plea.
For my soul is filled with troubles, and my life has drawn near to the realm of the dead.
I have been counted among those going down into the pit. I have become like a person with no helper, free among the dead.
Like the slain who have been cast down and lie in the graves, whom you no longer remember, they have been cut off from your hand.
They have placed me in the deepest pit, in darkness and the shadow of death.
Your anger has pressed heavily upon me, and you have brought all your troubles upon me. Pause.
You have made those who know me stay far from me. They have made me an object of disgust to them. I have been handed over and have not escaped.
My eye has grown weak from my misery. I have cried out to the Lord all day long. I have stretched out my hands to you.
Will you perform your wonders among the dead? Or will physicians rise up and praise you?
Will your mercy be proclaimed in the graves, and your faithfulness in destruction?
Will your wonders be known in the darkness, and your righteousness in a land you have forgotten?
But I have cried out to you, Lord, and my prayer will reach you early in the morning.
Why, Lord, will you abandon my soul? Do not turn your face away from me.
For I am poor and have been in distress since my youth. But when I was lifted up, I was humbled, and I rose again.
Your anger has come down upon me; your terrors have thrown me into turmoil.
They have surrounded me like water; together they have seized me all day long.
You have made my friends and those who know me stay far from me because of my misery.
The wisdom of Ethan the Israelite.
I will speak of the Lord’s mercies forever. From generation to generation I will proclaim your faithfulness with my mouth.
For you said, “Mercy will be built up forever; your faithfulness will be established in the heavens.”
I have established a covenant with my chosen ones; I have sworn to David my servant:
“I will establish your descendants forever; I will build up your throne from generation to generation.” Pause.
The heavens will reveal your wonders, Lord, and also your faithfulness in the assemblies of the holy ones.
For who among the clouds can compare with the Lord? And who among the sons of God can be like the Lord?
God, who is glorified in the council of the holy ones, is great and inspires fear in everyone around him.
Lord, God of hosts, who can be like you? You are mighty, Lord, and your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule over the might of the sea; you bring the motion of its waves to a stop.
You humbled the proud one like someone slain; with your mighty arm you scattered your enemies.
The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours. You laid the foundation of the inhabited world and everything that fills it.
You created the north and the sea; Tabor and Hermon will rejoice in your name.
Yours are the arm and the strength. Let your hand be strong, and let your right hand be lifted high.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; mercy and faithfulness will go before you.
Blessed are the people who know the shout of joy. Lord, they will walk in the light of your face.
They will rejoice in your name all day long, and they will be lifted up through your righteousness.
For you are the glory of their strength; our horn will be lifted high through your righteousness.
For the Lord is our protector; the Holy One of Israel is our king.
Then you spoke in a vision to your sons and said, “I have placed help upon a mighty man; I have raised up a chosen one from my people.”
I found David my servant; I anointed him with my holy oil.
My hand will support him, and my arm will strengthen him.
The enemy will not take advantage of him, and the son of lawlessness will not oppress him.
I will strike down his enemies before him, and I will destroy those who hate him.
My faithfulness and my mercy are with him, and his horn will be raised high in my name.
I will place his hand on the sea and his right hand on the rivers.
He will call to me, ‘You are my Father, my God, the protector of my salvation.’
And I will make him the firstborn, higher than all the kings of the earth.
I will preserve my mercy for him forever, and my covenant will be reliable for him.
I will establish his descendants forever and ever, and his throne like the days of heaven.
If his children abandon my law and do not walk according to my judgments,
if they despise my statutes and do not keep my commandments,
I will punish their lawless deeds with a rod and their sins with lashes.
I will not withdraw my mercy from them, nor will I betray my faithfulness.
Nor will I profane my covenant, and I will not reject what has come from my lips.
I have sworn once by my holiness that I will not lie to David.
His descendants will remain forever, and his throne will be like the sun before me,
like the moon, established forever, with the faithful witness in heaven. Pause.
But you have despised and cast down your anointed one; you have abandoned him, Lord.
You have destroyed the covenant with your servant; you have profaned his holiness down to the ground.
You have torn down all his walls; you have made his high places a terror.
Everyone who passes along the road has plundered him; he has become a mockery to his neighbors.
You have raised the right hand of his enemies; you have made all his enemies rejoice over him.
You have turned away the help of his sword; you have not supported him in battle.
You have stripped him of purity; you have struck his throne down to the ground.
You have shortened the days of his throne; you have poured shame upon him. Pause.
How long, Lord, will you turn away completely? Will your anger burn like fire?
Remember what my existence is. For did you create all human beings in vain?
Who is the person who will live and not see death, who will rescue his soul from the power of the underworld? Pause.
Where are your mercies of old, Lord, which you swore to David in your faithfulness?
Remember, Lord, the humiliation of your servants, for you helped a multitude of nations in your bosom.
These are the insults your enemies hurled, Lord, with which they mocked the change of your anointed one.
Blessed is the Lord forever. So shall it be! So shall it be!
The prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our refuge from generation to generation.
Before you established the mountains and formed the earth and the inhabited world, from eternity to eternity, you are.
Do not turn a person back to humiliation. And you said, “Return, children of men.”
For a thousand years before you are like a single day, like yesterday that has passed, and like a watch in the night.
Their years will become an object of contempt to them. They will pass away in the morning like grass.
In the morning they will blossom and pass away; in the evening they will fall, wither, and dry up.
For we have perished in your anger, and we have been troubled by your wrath.
You have placed our lawless deeds before you, and our lifetime before your face.
For all our days have perished; we have perished in your anger. Our years were considered like spiders.
The days of the years we live are seventy years, and if they exceed that, they are eighty. But the greater part of them is toil and suffering, for gentleness has come upon us, and we will be taught.
Who knows the power of your anger, and the terror of your wrath, so as to measure your strength?
Reveal yourself in this way to those instructed in wisdom in their hearts.
Return, Lord! How long? Be entreated on behalf of your servants.
For we were filled with your mercy in the morning throughout all our days, and we rejoiced and were glad,
in place of the days when you humbled us, the years in which they saw evils.
Look upon your servants and your works, and guide their children.
May the light of the Lord our God be upon us. Direct us according to the works of our hands. If you lie down in faith, at all times while you are in [?], you will be without evil.
The praise of the song of David. Whoever dwells in the help of the Most High will live in the shadow of the God of heaven.
He will say to the Lord, “You are the one who receives me, and my refuge, my God in whom I will trust.”
For he is the one who will rescue me from the hunters’ trap and from a harsh word.
He will shelter you beneath his breast, and you will trust beneath his wings. His faithfulness will surround you like armor.
You will not fear the terror of night or an arrow flying by day,
or anything that walks in darkness, or destruction and the demon at noon.
A thousand will fall on your left and ten thousand on your right, but they will not come near you.
You will only look your fill at them and see the repayment of sinners.
For you, Lord, are my hope. You have made the Most High your refuge.
No evil will come near you, and no plague will come near your dwelling.
For he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you on all your paths.
They will carry you on their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.
You will step upon a snake and a basilisk; you will trample a lion and a dragon.
Because he has trusted in me, I will rescue him. I will shelter him because he has known my name.
He will call out to me, and I will listen to him. I am with him in his distress, and I will rescue him and give him honor.
I will give him many days of life and show him my salvation.
A psalm of song for the Sabbath day.
It is good to give thanks to the Lord, to sing praises to your name, Most High,
to proclaim your mercy in the morning and your faithfulness each night,
on a ten-stringed harp and with a song on the lyre.
For you have made me glad, Lord, through what you have made, and I will rejoice in the works of your hands.
How great your works have grown, Lord! Your thoughts have multiplied exceedingly.
No senseless person will understand them, and anyone who is not wise will not know them.
When sinners spring up like grass, and all those who practice lawlessness have turned aside, it is so that they may be destroyed forever and ever.
But you, Lord, are exalted forever.
For look, your enemies will perish, and everyone who practices lawlessness will be scattered.
Let my horn be raised like that of a unicorn, and let my old age be anointed with rich oil.
My eye has looked its fill at my enemies, and my ear will hear about those who rise up against me and do evil.
The righteous person will rise like a palm tree and spread out like the cedar in Lebanon.
Planted in the house of God, they will flourish in the courtyards of our God.
Then they will flourish in a vigorous old age and speak with ease.
For the Lord our God is upright, and there is no injustice in him.

The praise of David’s song, for the day before the Sabbath, when the land was settled. The Lord reigns; he has clothed himself in splendor. The Lord has clothed himself in strength and girded himself with it. Indeed, he has established the inhabited world so that it will not be shaken.
Your throne has been established from eternity; you have existed from eternity.
Lord, the rivers have risen; the rivers have raised their voices above the roar of the many waters.
The towering waves of the sea are wonderful; the Lord is wonderful on high.
Your testimonies have been firmly confirmed. Holiness befits your house, Lord, for days without end.
A psalm of David, for the fourth day of the week. The Lord is the God of vengeance; the God of vengeance has revealed himself openly.
Rise up, you who judge the earth; repay the proud as they deserve.
How long, Lord, will sinners—how long will sinners boast?
They will answer and speak mockingly; all who practice lawlessness will speak.
Lord, they have humbled your people and oppressed your inheritance.
They have killed the widow and the resident foreigner; they have murdered the orphans.
And they have said, “The Lord will not see, and the God of Jacob will not know.”
Understand, then, you senseless people among the people! You fools, come to your senses!
Does the one who planted the ear not hear? Or does the one who formed the eye not see you?
Will the one who disciplines the nations not rebuke—the one who teaches people knowledge?
The Lord knows that people’s thoughts are empty.
Blessed is the person whom you instruct, Lord, and teach from your law,
so that he may have relief from evil days, until a pit is dug for the sinner.
For the Lord will not abandon his people, nor will he forget his inheritance,
until righteousness returns to judgment, and all who are upright in heart draw near to it. Pause.
Who will rise up with me against the wicked? Or who will stand with me against those who practice lawlessness?
If the Lord had not helped me, my soul would soon have settled in the realm of the dead.
Whenever I say, “My foot has slipped,” your mercy, Lord, comes to my aid.
Lord, as the troubles in my heart multiplied, your consolations gladdened my soul.
Can a throne of lawlessness remain beside you, one that creates suffering through a decree?
They will plot against the life of the righteous person and condemn innocent blood.
The Lord has become a refuge for me, and God a help for my hope.
He will repay them for their lawlessness, and the Lord our God will destroy them in their wickedness.
The praise of the song of David. Come, let us rejoice in the Lord; let us shout joyfully to God our salvation.
Let us come before him with thanksgiving; let us shout joyfully to him with psalms.
For the Lord our God is great, and he is a great king over all the gods.
For all the ends of the earth are in his hand, and the mountain heights are his.
The sea is his, and he made it; his hands formed the dry land.
Come, let us worship and bow down to him; let us weep before the Lord who made us.
For he is our God, and we—we are his people and the sheep of his hand. Today, if you hear his voice,
do not harden your hearts as in the days of provocation, as on the day of testing in the wilderness,
when your ancestors put me to the test and tried me, and saw my deeds.
I hated this generation for forty years, and I said, “They always go astray in their hearts, and they have not known my ways.”
As I swore in my anger, “They will enter my place of rest.”
The song of David, when the house was to be built after the captivity. Sing a new song to the Lord; all the earth, sing to the Lord.
Sing to the Lord and bless his name; proclaim his salvation from day to day.
Tell of his glory among the nations and his wonders among all the peoples.
For the Lord is great and greatly blessed; he is greater than all the gods.
For all the gods of the nations are demonic idols, but the Lord made the heavens.
Splendor and beauty are before him; purity and greatness are in his holy places.
Families of the nations, bring to the Lord; bring glory and honor to the Lord.
Bring glory to the name of the Lord; carry the sacrifices and enter his courts.
Worship the Lord in his holy courtyard. Let the whole earth tremble before him.
Say to the nations, “The Lord has reigned from the tree.” For he has also established the inhabited world so that it will not be shaken. He will judge the peoples fairly and the nations in his anger.
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad. The sea and all that fills it will stir; the fields and everything in them will rejoice.
Then all the trees of the field will rejoice
before the Lord, because he is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with his truth.
A psalm of David, when his land was established. The Lord reigns. Let the earth rejoice; let the many islands be glad.
Cloud and darkness surround him. Righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.
Fire will go before him and burn up his enemies around him.
His lightning lit up the world. The earth saw it and trembled.
The mountains melted like wax before the Lord, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens proclaimed his righteousness, and all the peoples saw his glory.
All who worship objects carved by hand will be put to shame, those who boast in their idols. Worship him, all his angels.
Zion heard and was glad, and the daughters of Judea rejoiced because of your judgments, Lord.
For you, Lord, are exalted above all the earth. You are exalted far above all the gods.
You who love the Lord, hate evil. He will guard the souls of his holy ones; he will rescue them from the hand of sinners.
Light has dawned for the righteous, and joy for those who are upright in heart.
You righteous people, rejoice in the Lord and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
A psalm of David. Sing a new song to the Lord, because the Lord does wondrous things. His right hand and his holy arm have brought him victory.
The Lord has made his salvation known. He has revealed his righteousness before the nations.
He remembered his mercy toward Jacob and his truth toward the house of Israel. All the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
All the earth, shout joyfully to God. Sing, rejoice, and sing praises to him.
Sing praises to him with a lyre, with a lyre and the sound of a psalm.
With hammered trumpets and the sound of a horn, shout joyfully before the King, the Lord.
Let the sea be stirred, and everything in it, the world and those who live in it.
The rivers will clap their hands together.
The mountains will rejoice because he has come to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with fairness.
A psalm of David. The Lord reigns; let the peoples rage. He sits upon the cherubim; let the earth shake.
The Lord is great in Zion. He is exalted above all the peoples.
Let them praise your great name, for it is awe-inspiring and holy.
And a king’s honor is to love justice. You established uprightness; you are the one who carried out justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the Lord our God and worship at the footstool of his feet.
For holy Moses and Aaron were among his priests, and Samuel was among those who called on his name. They cried out to the Lord, and he listened to them.
He spoke with them in a pillar of cloud. They kept his testimonies and the commands he gave them.
Lord our God, you are the one who listened to them. God, you are the one who forgave them, but you took vengeance for all their deeds.
Exalt the Lord our God and worship at his holy mountain, for the Lord our God is holy.
A psalm of thanksgiving. Shout joyfully to the Lord, all the earth.
Serve the Lord with gladness. Come into his presence with rejoicing.
Know that the Lord himself is our God. He is the one who made us, not we ourselves. We are his people and the sheep of his pasture.
Enter his gates with rejoicing and his courtyards. Give thanks to him with songs of praise, and bless his name, for
the Lord our God is good, for his mercy lasts forever, and his faithfulness lasts from generation to generation.
A psalm of David. I will sing to you, Lord, of mercy and justice.
I will sing praises and gain understanding in the way of the holy. When will the Lord God come to me? I walked with innocence of heart within my house.
I did not set any lawless deed before me. I hated those who commit transgressions. A crooked heart did not cling to me.
When the wicked person turned away from me, I did not know him.
I cast out the one who secretly slandered his neighbor. I did not eat with anyone who had haughty eyes and an insatiable heart.
My eyes watch over the holy people of the land, so that they may dwell with me. The one who walked in the way of the holy was the one who served me.
The one who acted arrogantly did not live within my house. I did not let the one who spoke unjustly stand before my eyes.
In the morning I killed all the sinners of the land, to wipe out from the city of the Lord all those who practice lawlessness.
The prayer of the poor person when he is distressed and pours out his plea before the Lord.
Lord, listen to my prayer, and let my cry come to you.
Do not turn your face away from me. Turn your ear toward me on the day when I am distressed. Listen to me quickly on the day when I cry out to you.
For my days have vanished like smoke, and my bones have been scorched like a stone.
I have been struck down like grass, and my heart has dried up, for I forgot to eat my bread.
Because of the day of my groaning, my bones clung to my flesh.
I have become like a pelican in the wilderness; I have become like an owl in a house.
I spent the night keeping watch; I became like a bird alone on a rooftop.
My enemies mocked me all day long, and those who honored me swore by me.
For I ate ashes instead of my bread, and I mixed what I drink with tears.
Because of your anger and your wrath, for you lifted me up and threw me down.
My days declined like a shadow, and I withered like grass.
But you, Lord, remain forever, and your remembrance lasts from generation to generation.
Rise up and have compassion on Zion, for the time has come for you to have compassion on her; the appointed time has arrived.
For your servants loved her stones, and they will have compassion on her dust.
Then the nations will fear the name of the Lord, and the kings of the earth will fear your glory.
For the Lord will rebuild Zion and reveal his glory.
He looked upon the prayer of the humble and did not despise their plea.
Let this be written for another generation, and the people who will be created will praise the Lord.
For he looked out from his holy height; the Lord looked out from heaven upon the earth,
to hear the groaning of the prisoners, to release the children of those who were killed,
to proclaim the name of the Lord in Zion and his praise in Jerusalem,
when the peoples gather together in one place, and the kings gather to serve the Lord.
He answered him in the course of his strength: “Tell me how few my days are.
Do not bring me down halfway through my days. Your years last through generation after generation.
From the beginning, you, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will perish, but you remain. They will all wear out like a garment, and you will roll them up like a cloak, and they will be changed.
But you remain the same, and your years will not end.”
The children of your servants will live on the earth, and their descendants will be established forever.
Of David. My soul, praise the Lord, and everything within me, praise his holy name.
My soul, praise the Lord, and do not forget all his benefits:
He forgives all your sins and heals all your diseases.
He rescues your life from destruction and crowns you with mercy and compassion.
He satisfies your desire with good things; your youth will be renewed like an eagle’s.
The Lord performs acts of mercy and brings justice to everyone who suffers oppression.
He made his ways known to Moses and his wishes to the children of Israel.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in mercy.
He will not stay angry to the end, nor will he be wrathful forever.
He has not dealt with us according to our sins or repaid us according to our lawless deeds.
For as high as heaven is above the earth, the Lord has made his mercy strong toward those who fear him.
As far as the east is from the west, he has removed our lawless deeds from us.
As a father has compassion on his children, the Lord has had compassion on those who fear him.
For he knows how we are formed. Remember, Lord, that we are dust.
A person's days are like grass; he flourishes like a flower of the field.
For his spirit has left him, and he no longer exists, nor does he return to know his place.
But the Lord's mercy is from eternity to eternity upon those who fear him.
And his righteousness is upon the children's children of those who keep his covenant and remember his commandments in order to carry them out.
The Lord has established his throne in heaven, and his kingdom rules over everyone.
Bless the Lord, all his angels, mighty in strength, who carry out his word, listening to the voice of his words.
Bless the Lord, all his heavenly forces, his servants who do his will.
Bless the Lord, all his works, in every place under his rule. My soul, bless the Lord.
Of David. My soul, bless the Lord. Lord, Lord my God, you have become exceedingly great.
You have clothed yourself in splendor and beauty. He has wrapped himself in light like a garment; he has stretched out heaven like a curtain.
He waters his upper chambers with water, making the clouds something for him to ride upon. He walks upon the wings of the winds.
He makes his angels [?] and his servants a flame of fire.
