He firmly established the foundations of the earth; it will not be moved forever and ever.
He covered it with the deep like a garment; the waters stood above the mountains.
They will flee at your rebuke and grow weak at the sound of your thunder.
The mountains rise and the plains sink down in their places, which you established for them.
You set a boundary for them that they cannot cross, nor can they return to cover the earth.
He sends springs into the watercourses; the waters flow between the mountains.
They give drink to all the wild animals of the field; the wild donkeys drink from them to quench their thirst.
The birds of the sky settle on them and sing among the rocks.
He waters the mountains from his lofty places. The earth will be filled with the fruit of his works.
He makes grass grow for the livestock and plants for people to cultivate, to bring bread out of the earth.
Wine gladdens the human heart, oil makes the face shine, and bread strengthens the human heart.
The trees of the field will drink their fill, the cedars of Lebanon that you planted.
Sparrows nest in them. The heron's home is high above them.
You gave the high mountains to the deer and the rocks as a refuge for the hares.
You appointed the moon for the seasons. The sun knows its setting place.
You made darkness, and night came. All the wild animals of the field will roam in it.
The young lions roar to seize their prey and seek their food from God.
The sun rose, and they gathered together and lay down in their dens. A person went out to work
and to labor until evening.
How numerous your works have become, Lord! You made them all with wisdom. The earth is filled with your creation.
This great, wide sea contains countless creatures, living things both small and large.
Ships sail on it. There is the dragon that you formed to play with.
They all look to you to give them their food at the proper time.
When you give to them, they will gather it. When you open your hand, they will all be satisfied with your goodness.
When you turn your face away, they will be troubled. You will take away their breath, and they will perish and return to their earth.
You will send your Spirit, and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth again.
May the glory of the Lord endure forever. The Lord will rejoice in his works.
He looks at the earth and makes it tremble. He touches the mountains, and they give off smoke.
I will sing to the Lord throughout my life. I will sing praises to my God as long as I exist.
My words will be sweet to him, and I will rejoice in the Lord. May sinners perish from the earth
and the lawless cease to exist. My soul, bless the Lord!
Hallelujah! Give thanks to the Lord, call on his name, and proclaim his works among the nations.
Sing to him, sing praises to him, and tell of all his wonders.
Take pride in his holy name. Let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
Seek the Lord and gain strength; seek his face at all times.
Remember the wonders he has done, his works and the judgments of his mouth.
You descendants of Abraham, his servants, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is the Lord our God; his judgments are throughout the whole earth.
He has remembered his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations.
The covenant he established with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac.
He established it for Jacob as a decree, and for Israel as an everlasting covenant.
He said, “I will give you the land of Canaan as the measured allotment of your inheritance.”
When they were few in number, few and living as foreigners in it.
They went from nation to nation, and from another kingdom to another people.
He allowed no one to oppress them; he rebuked kings for their sake.
“Do not touch my anointed ones; do not harm my prophets.”
He called for a famine upon the land; he broke the support that bread provides.
He sent a man ahead of them; Joseph was sold as a slave.
They humbled his feet with bronze shackles; his soul passed through iron.
Until his word came to pass, the word of the Lord refined him.
The king sent and released him; the ruler of the peoples set him free.
He appointed him lord over his house and ruler over everything he owned.
To teach his rulers in his own way and instruct his elders.
Israel went down to Egypt; Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
He greatly increased his people and made them stronger than their enemies.
He turned his heart to hate his people and to deal deceitfully with his servants.
He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
He placed among them the words of his signs, and his wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness and covered them; and he rejected his words.
He turned their waters into blood and killed their fish.
Their land brought forth frogs in the chambers of their kings.
He spoke, and dogflies came, and frogs throughout their territory.
He turned their rain into hail, with fire blazing in their land.
He struck their grapevines and their fig trees.
He shattered every tree in their territory. He spoke, and locusts came, and young locusts beyond counting.
It ate all the vegetation in their land.
He struck down every firstborn in their land, the first fruits of all their labor.
He brought them out with silver and gold, and there was no one weak among their tribes.
Egypt rejoiced at their departure, because fear of them had fallen upon Egypt.
He spread out a cloud to shade them, and a fire to give them light at night.
They asked for flies, and a flock of quail came to them. He satisfied them with bread from heaven.
He split a rock, and water poured out; rivers flowed through places where there was no water.
For he remembered his holy word, which he had established with Abraham his servant.
He [?] his people out with rejoicing, and his chosen ones with joy.
He gave them the lands of the nations, and they inherited the fruits of the peoples’ labor.
So that they would keep his decrees and seek his law.
Hallelujah! Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, and his mercy lasts forever.
Who can tell of the Lord’s mighty deeds and make all his praises heard?
Blessed are those who uphold justice and do what is right at all times.
Remember us, Lord, with the favor you show your people, and visit us with your salvation.
So that we may see the prosperity of your chosen ones, rejoice in the joy of your nation, and receive honor together with your inheritance.
For we have sinned along with our ancestors; we have acted lawlessly and violently.
Our ancestors did not understand your wonders in Egypt. They did not remember your abundant mercy, and they rebelled as they came up through the Red Sea.
And they were saved for the sake of his name, to reveal his power.
He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up. He led them through the depths as through a desert.
He saved them from the hand of those who hated them, and they were redeemed from the hand of the enemy.
The water covered those who oppressed them; not one of them remained.
They believed his words and sang his praise.
They quickly forgot his deeds and did not wait for his counsel.
They craved intensely in the wilderness and tested God in a place where there was no water.
He gave them what they wanted and sent satisfaction to their souls.
They were jealous of Moses in the camp and of Aaron, the Lord’s holy one.
The earth opened and swallowed Dathan and covered Abiram’s assembly.
A fire blazed in their assembly, and a flame burned up the sinners.
They made a calf at Horeb and worshiped what their hands had made.
They exchanged their glory for the image of a calf that [?] grass. They forgot God, who saves them.
The one who did those great things in Egypt, those wonders in the land of Ham,
terrifying things at the Red Sea.
He said he would destroy them, but Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him to turn away his anger so that he would not destroy them.
They despised the good land and did not believe his words.
They grumbled in their dwellings and did not listen to the Lord’s voice.
He raised his hand against them to strike them down in the wilderness.
To kill their descendants among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands.
They served Baal-peor and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
They provoked him with their deeds, and destruction spread among them.
Phinehas stood up and pleaded on their behalf, and the destruction stopped.
It was counted to him as righteousness for generation after generation, forever.
They provoked him at the water of dispute, and Moses suffered because of them,
because they provoked his spirit, and he gave them orders with his lips.
They did not destroy the nations as the Lord had told them.
They mingled with the nations and learned their ways.
They became slaves to what their hands had made, and it became a stumbling block for them.
They sacrificed their sons and daughters to the worthless one and poured out innocent blood.
Their blood, the blood of their sons and daughters, to the demons [?]; they sacrificed to the handmade idols of Canaan and filled the land with blood.
They defiled themselves through their deeds and prostituted themselves through the thoughts of their hearts.
My Lord became angry with his people and loathed his inheritance.
He handed them over to their enemies, and those who hated them ruled over them.
Their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought low under their hands.
He rescued them many times, but they provoked him with their plans and were brought low because of their lawless deeds.
He saw them when they were oppressed.
When he heard their plea, he remembered his covenant and relented because of his abundant mercy.
They were shown compassion by all who had taken them captive.
Save us, Lord our God, and gather us from among our enemies, so that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in praising you.
Blessed is the Lord, the Holy One, the God of Israel, from eternity to eternity. And let all the people say, “So be it! So be it!”
Hallelujah! Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy lasts forever.
Let those whom the Lord has redeemed say this, those whom he redeemed from the hands of their enemies.
He gathered them from the lands, from the east and the west, from the north and the sea.
They wandered in the wilderness, in a place without water. They did not find the way to a city where they could live.
They were hungry and thirsty, and their souls grew faint within them.
They cried out to the Lord, and he heard them when they were suffering. He rescued them from their distress.
He led them along a straight road so that they could go to a city where they could live.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders for humanity.
For he satisfied the empty soul and filled the hungry soul with good things.
Those who sat in darkness and the shadow of death, bound in poverty and iron,
because they rebelled against the word of God and defied the counsel of the Most High.
Their hearts were humbled by hardships. They grew weak, and there was no one to help them.
They cried out to the Lord when they were suffering, and he rescued them from their distress.
He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death and tore apart their bonds.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders for humanity.
For he shattered gates of bronze and broke bars of iron.
He took them into his care on the path of their lawlessness, for they had been brought low because of their lawless deeds.
Their hearts recoiled from all food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
They cried out to the Lord when they were suffering, and he rescued them from their distress.
He sent his word and healed them. He saved them from their hardships.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders for humanity.
Let them offer a sacrifice of praise and tell of his deeds with joy.
Those who go down to the sea in their ships, doing business on the great waters.
They are the ones who saw the Lord’s deeds and his wonders in the deep.
He spoke, and a storm wind arose, and its waves rose high.
They go up to the heavens and come down to the depths; their souls melted away amid their troubles.
They were shaken and staggered like someone who is drunk, and all their wisdom failed them.
They cried out to the Lord in their distress, and he rescued them from their troubles.
He struck the storm, and the wind became calm, and its waves fell silent.
They rejoiced because they had become quiet, and he guided them to the harbors they desired.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders for humanity.
Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people and praise him among the seated elders.
He turned rivers into a desert and springs of water into dry ground.
He turned fruitful land into salty ground because of the wickedness of those who lived in it.
He turned a desert into pools of water and a waterless land into springs of water.
He made the hungry settle there and established it as a city to live in.
They sowed fields and planted vineyards, and they produced a fruitful harvest.
He blessed them, and they multiplied greatly. He did not let their livestock decrease.
They dwindled and suffered because of oppression, troubles, hardship, and turmoil.
He poured contempt on rulers and made them wander in a desert where there was no road.
He helped the needy in their poverty and established families like sheep.
The upright will see and rejoice, and all lawlessness will shut its mouth.
Who is wise? Let him keep these things, and let them understand the Lord’s mercies.
A song, a psalm of David.
God, my heart is ready; my heart is ready. I will sing and make music in your glory.
Awake, harp and lyre! I will rise early.
I will praise you among the peoples, Lord; I will sing to you among the nations.
For your mercy is great above the heavens, and your faithfulness reaches to your clouds.
Rise high above the heavens, God, and let your glory be over the whole earth.
So that your beloved ones may be rescued, save me with your right hand and listen to me.
God spoke in his temple: “I will be exalted. I will divide Shechem and measure out the valley of settlements.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim is the protection of my head; Judah is my king.
Moab is the basin of my hope. I will cast my sandal upon Edom, and the Philistines will submit to me.”
Who will lead me to Edom? Or who will bring me to the fortified city?
Is it not you, God, who abandoned us? Yet you do not go out with our armies, God.
Give us help in our distress, for human deliverance is worthless.
With our God we will act mightily, and he will trample all our enemies.
For the end. A psalm of David. God, do not remain silent concerning my praise.
For the mouth of the sinner and the mouth of deceit have opened against me. They have spoken against me with a deceitful tongue.
They surrounded me with words of hatred and fought against me without cause. Instead of
loving me, they accused me, but I was praying.
They prepared evil against me in place of good, and hatred in place of my love.
Appoint a sinner over him, and let the devil stand at his right hand.
When he is judged, let him come out condemned. Let his prayer become a sin for him.
Let his days be few, and let someone else take his office of oversight.
Let his children become orphans and his wife a widow.
Let his children be driven out to wander and beg. Let them be thrown out of their homes.
Let the creditor search out everything he owns, and let strangers plunder the fruits of his labor.
Let there be no one to take him in, and let there be no one to have compassion on his orphans.
Let his children be wiped out, and let his name be erased in a single generation.
Let the lawless deeds of his ancestors be remembered before the Lord, and let his mother’s sin not be erased.
Let them remain before the Lord at all times, and let his memory be wiped from the earth.
Because he did not remember to show mercy, but pursued the needy, the poor, and the brokenhearted to put them to death.
He loved a curse, and it will come upon him. He did not want a blessing, and it will flee from him.
He put on the curse like a garment. It entered his inward parts like water and his bones like oil.
Let it be to him like the garment he wraps around himself and like a belt he always fastens around himself.
This is the reward from the Lord for those who accuse me and speak evil against my soul.
But you, Lord, Lord, deal mercifully with me for the sake of your name, for your mercy is good.
Save me, for I am poor and needy, and my heart is troubled within me.
I have vanished like a fading shadow; I have been shaken off like locusts.
My knees have grown weak from fasting, and my flesh has changed because of oil.
I have become an object of ridicule to them. They saw me and shook their heads.
Help me, Lord my God; save me according to your mercy.
Let them know that this is your hand, and that you, Lord, have done it.
They will curse, but you will bless. Those who rise up against me will be put to shame, but your servant will rejoice.
Let those who accuse me put on shame and wrap themselves in it like a cloak.
I will greatly praise my Lord, and I will bless him with my mouth in the midst of a multitude.
For he stood at the right hand of the poor, to save my soul from those who pursue me.
A psalm of David. The Lord said to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies beneath your feet.”
The Lord has sent you from Zion as a rod of power, and you will rule in the midst of your enemies.
Your authority is with you in the abundance of your power, in the splendor of the holy ones. From the womb I begot you before the morning star.
The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
The Lord at your right hand will crush kings on the day of his anger.
He will judge the nations and fill them with slaughter. He will crush their heads across the vast earth.
He will drink water from a torrent along the way; therefore he will lift up my head.
Hallelujah. I will praise you, Lord, with all my heart, in the council of the upright and in the assembly.
The works of the Lord are great, examined in all his desires.
His work is praise and splendor, and his righteousness endures forever and ever.
He caused his wonders to be remembered. The Lord is merciful and compassionate.
He gave food to those who fear him. He will remember his covenant forever.
He declared the power of his works to his people, to give them the inheritance of the nations.
The works of his hands are truth and justice; all his commandments are trustworthy.
They are firmly established forever and ever, made in truth and uprightness.
He sent redemption to his people; he ordained his covenant forever. His name is holy and awe-inspiring.
The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom. Understanding is good for everyone who practices it. His praise endures forever and ever.
Hallelujah. Blessed is the person who fears the Lord and greatly delights in his commandments.
His descendants will be mighty on the earth; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Glory and wealth are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever and ever.
Light has dawned in the darkness for the upright. The Lord God is merciful, compassionate, and righteous.
The compassionate and generous man is good. He will manage his words with justice.
For he will never be shaken. The righteous man will be remembered forever.
He will not be afraid of bad news. His heart is ready to trust in the Lord.
His heart is firm, and he will not be afraid until he has looked his fill at his enemies.
He has distributed freely; he has given to the poor. His righteousness endures forever and ever, and his horn will be raised in glory.
The sinner will see and be angry. He will grind his teeth and waste away. The desire of sinners will perish.
Hallelujah. Company of servants, praise the Lord; praise the name of the Lord.
May the name of the Lord be blessed from now on and forever.
And from eternity to eternity, from the east to the west, praise the name of the Lord.
The Lord is exalted above all the nations; his glory is in the heavens.
Who is like the Lord our God?
He dwells on high and looks upon the lowly things in heaven and on earth.
He raises the poor from the ground and lifts the needy from the dung heap,
to seat him with the rulers of his people.
He makes a barren woman dwell in her home as a joyful mother of children.
Alleluia. The chorus. When Israel came out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign speech.
Judea became his sanctuary; Israel ruled over her.
The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back.
The mountains leaped like rams, and the hills like lambs.
What happened to you, sea, that you fled, and to you, Jordan, that you turned back?
Mountains, why did you leap like rams, and hills, like lambs?
The earth shook before the Lord, before the God of Jacob,
who turned the rock into pools of water and the hard stone into springs of water.
Not to us, Lord, not to us, but give glory to your name because of your mercy and your truth,
so that the nations do not say, “Where is their God?”
But our God is above in the heavens and on earth. He has done everything he wishes. Hallelujah.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
They have eyes, but they do not see.
They have ears, but they do not hear. They have mouths, but they cannot speak. They have noses, but they cannot smell.
They have hands, but they cannot feel. They have feet, but they cannot walk. They cannot make a sound with their throats, for there is no breath in their mouths.
Those who made them will become like them, as will everyone who trusts in them.
The house of Israel has put its hope in the Lord. He is their helper and their protector.
The house of Aaron has put its hope in the Lord. He is their helper and their protector.
Those who fear the Lord have put their hope in the Lord. He is their helper and their protector.
The Lord has remembered us and blessed us. He will bless the house of Israel; he will bless the house of Aaron.
He will bless everyone who fears the Lord, both small and great.
The Lord will increase our numbers, ours and our children's.
We are blessed by the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
The heaven of heaven belongs to the Lord, but he gave the earth to human beings.
It is not the dead who will bless you, Lord, nor anyone who goes down to the underworld.
But we, the living, will bless the Lord from now on and forever.
Hallelujah. I loved this: that the Lord will hear the sound of my plea.
Because he has turned his ear toward me, I will call out to him throughout my days.
The cords of death seized me, and the dangers of the underworld overtook me. I encountered distress and suffering.
I called on the name of the Lord: "O Lord, rescue my soul."
The Lord is merciful and righteous, and our God shows mercy.
The Lord protects little children. I was brought low, and the Lord saved me.
My soul returned to rest, because the Lord has done good to me.
For he rescued my soul from death, my eyes from weeping, and my feet from slipping.
I will please the Lord in the land of the living.
Hallelujah.
I believed; therefore I spoke. But I was greatly humbled.
I said in my alarm, “All people are liars.”
What will I repay the Lord for all that he has done for me?
I will take the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord.
The death of the Lord’s holy ones is precious in his sight.
O Lord, I am your servant; I am the son of your maidservant. You have loosened my bonds.
I will offer you a sacrifice of praise.
I will fulfill my vows to the Lord in the courtyards of the house of our God, before all the people,
in your midst, Jerusalem.
Hallelujah. All nations, praise the Lord! All peoples, praise him!
For his mercy toward us has grown strong, and the Lord’s truth endures forever and ever.
Hallelujah. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy lasts forever.
Let the house of Israel say, “He is good, for his mercy lasts forever.”
Let the house of Aaron say, “His mercy lasts forever.”
Let everyone who fears the Lord say, “His mercy lasts forever.”
I cried out to the Lord in distress, and he heard me in a spacious place.
The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can a person do to me?
The Lord is my helper; I will feast my eyes on my enemies.
It is better to trust in the Lord than to trust in a person.
It is better to put your confidence in the Lord than to put your confidence in a ruler.
All the nations surrounded me; I repelled them in the name of the Lord.
They surrounded me on every side, but I repelled them in the name of the Lord.
They surrounded me like swarming honeycombs of bees, and they blazed like a fire among thorns. But I repelled them in the name of the Lord.
They pushed [?] to make me fall, and the Lord helped me.
The Lord is my strength and my praise; he has become my salvation.
The sound of rejoicing and salvation is in the dwellings of the righteous. The Lord’s right hand has been raised high.
The Lord’s right hand has acted mightily.
I will not die, but I will live and tell of the Lord’s deeds, for his mercy lasts forever.
The Lord disciplined me severely, but he did not hand me over to death.
Open the gates of righteousness for me, so that I may enter through them and give thanks to the Lord.
This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous are those who enter through it.
I will give thanks to you, Lord, because you heard me and became my salvation.
The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This came about through the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes.
This is the day that the Lord has made. Let us gather together, rejoice, and be glad in it.
O Lord, save us! O Lord, bless us!
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord. We have blessed you from the house of the Lord.
God, the Lord, has appeared to us. Celebrate a festival with leafy branches, up to the horns of the altar.
You are my God; I will give thanks to you. You are my God; I will exalt you. I will give thanks to you because you heard me and became my salvation.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy lasts forever.
Hallelujah. A — Aleph. Blessed are those who are holy in their way, who walk in the law of the Lord.
Blessed are those who study his testimonies, who seek him with their whole heart.
For those who have walked in his ways do not practice lawlessness.
You commanded that your commandments be kept diligently.
If only my ways would be made straight, so that I might keep your statutes!
I would not be put to shame when I looked upon your commandments.
I will give thanks to you with an upright heart as I learn your righteous judgments.
I will keep the statutes. Do not abandon me completely.
B — Beth. How can a young man make his way straight? By keeping your words.
I have sought you with my whole heart. Do not cast me away from your commandments.
I have hidden your words in my heart so that I will not sin against you.
Blessed are you, Lord. Teach me your statutes.
With my lips I have declared all the judgments of your mouth.
I have rejoiced in the way of your testimonies as in every kind of wealth.
I will meditate on your commandments and examine your ways.
I will meditate on your statutes and not forget your words.
3 — Gimel. Reward your servant; I will live and keep your words.
Open my eyes so that I may see the wonders in your law.
I am a stranger on the earth. Do not hide your commandments from me.
My soul has longed for your judgments at all times.
You have rebuked the proud. Those who turn away from your commandments are cursed.
Take away my disgrace and contempt, because I have sought your testimonies.
For even rulers sat and spoke against me, but your servant was meditating on your statutes.
For indeed, your testimonies are my meditations, and your statutes are my counselors.
4 — Daleth. My soul has clung to the ground. Give me life according to your word.
I told you my ways, and you listened to me. Teach me your statutes.
And show me your way, and I will meditate on your wonders.
My soul has spent the night awake because of my sorrow. Strengthen me through your words.
Remove the way of injustice from me, and have mercy on me through your law.
For I have desired the way of your truth. I have set your judgments before me and have not forgotten them.
I have clung to your testimonies, Lord. Do not put me to shame.
I ran in the way of your commandments when you broadened my heart.
5 — He. Instruct me, Lord, in the way of your statutes, so that I may seek them at all times.
Teach me so that I may study your law and keep it with all my heart.
Lead me in the way of your commandments, because that is what I have desired.
Turn my heart toward your testimonies and not toward injustice.
Turn my eyes away so that they do not look at what is worthless. Give me life in your way.
Confirm your word to your servant, who is coming to fear you.
Take away the disgrace that I have thought about, for your judgments are sweet.
Look, I have desired your commandments.
6 — Waw. Give me life through your righteousness. Let your mercy come down upon me, Lord, salvation together with your word.
Then I will answer those who reproach me, because I have placed my hope in your words.
Do not take the word of truth completely from my mouth, for I have trusted in your judgments.
And I will keep your law at all times, forever and ever.
I walked in a wide-open place, for I sought your commandments.
And I spoke of your testimonies before kings without being ashamed.
And I meditated on your commandments, which I loved very much.
I lifted my hands to your commandments, which I loved, and I pondered your statutes.
7 — Zayin. Remember your word to your servant, in which I have placed my hope.
This comforted me in my humiliation, for your word gave me life.
The proud broke the law greatly, but I did not turn away from your law.
I remembered your judgments from long ago, Lord, and I was comforted.
Anguish gripped me because of the sinners who abandon your law.
Your statutes are songs for me in the place where I live as a stranger.
I remembered your name at night; I kept your law.
This happened to me because I sought your statutes.
8 — Heth. You are my portion, Lord. I said that I would keep your word.
I pleaded for your favor with all my heart.
Have mercy on me according to your word, for I have thought about your ways. Turn my feet toward your testimonies.
I made myself ready and was not troubled about keeping your commandments.
The cords of sinners entangled me, but I did not forget your law.
I used to rise at midnight to proclaim the words of righteousness.
I am a companion of everyone who fears you and keeps your commandments.
The earth is full of your mercy, Lord. Teach me your statutes.
9 — Teth. Lord, you have shown kindness to your servant.
Lord, according to your word, teach me goodness, instruction, and knowledge, for I have believed in your commandments.
I sinned before you humbled me; therefore I kept your words.
You are good. Teach me your statutes in your goodness.
The violence of the proud has increased against me, but I will seek your ways with all my heart.
Their heart has grown thick like fat, but I have meditated on your law.
It is good for me that you humbled me, so that I might understand your statutes.
The law from your mouth is better to me than thousands of pieces of silver and gold.
10 — Yod. Your hands formed me and made me. Teach me so that I may understand your commandments.
Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, because I have trusted your words.
I know, Lord, that your judgments are righteous and that you humbled me in truth.
Let your mercy comfort me, according to your word to your servant.
Let your mercies reach me so that I may live, because your law is my meditation.
Let the proud be put to shame, because they have wronged me with violence, but I meditate on your commandments.
Let those who fear you turn to me, along with those who know your wonders.
Let my heart be pure in your statutes, so that I will not be put to shame.
11 — Kaph. My soul has grown faint longing for your salvation; I have put my hope in your word.
My eyes have grown weary looking for your word. When will you comfort me?
For I have become like a wineskin in the frost, but I have not forgotten your statutes.
How many are the days of your servant? When will you carry out judgment for me against those who pursue me?
The lawless have spoken to me of troubles, but this is not the way of your law.
All your commandments are true. They have pursued me with violence; help me.
He nearly wiped me off the earth, but I did not abandon your commandments.
Give me life according to your mercy, and I will keep the testimonies of your mouth.
12 — Lamed. Lord, your word remains in heaven forever.
And your truth lasts from generation to generation. You laid the foundation of the earth, and it remains.
The day continues according to your decree, for they are all your servants.
If your law had not been my meditation, I would have perished in my humiliation.
I will never forget your statutes, because through them you gave me life, Lord.
I am yours, Lord; save me, because I have sought your statutes.
Sinners have waited for me to destroy me; they have not understood your testimonies.
I have seen the end of every completed thing.
13 — Mem. Your commandment is exceedingly broad. How I have loved your name, Lord! It has been my meditation all day long.
You have made me wiser than my enemies through your commandments, for they are mine forever.
You have made me wiser than all my teachers, for your testimonies are what I meditate on.
For I sought your commandments. I became wiser than the elders, for I sought your testimonies.
I have kept my feet away from every evil path so that I may keep your words.
I have not turned away from your testimonies, for you yourself have laid down the law for me.
Your words have become sweet to my palate, sweeter than honey in my mouth.
I have understood your commandments. Therefore I have hated every path of injustice, for you yourself have laid down the law for me.
14 — Nun. Your word is the lamp for my feet and the light for my paths.
I have sworn and confirmed it: I will keep your righteous judgments.
I have been greatly humbled. Lord, give me life according to your word.
Lord, accept what comes from my mouth, and teach me your judgments.
My life is in my hands at all times, and I have not forgotten your law.
Sinners have set a trap for me, and I have not forgotten your commandments.
I have inherited your testimonies forever, for they are the joy of my heart.
I have inclined my heart to carry out your decrees for an everlasting reward.
15 — Samekh. I have hated the lawless person; I have loved your law.
You are my helper and the one who receives me. I have trusted in your word.
Go away from me, you who do evil, and I will examine the commandments of my God.
Take me into your care according to your word, so that I may live. Do not put me to shame because of what I hope for.
Help me so that I may be saved, and I will meditate on your decrees at all times.
You have despised everyone who strays from your decrees, for their thinking is unjust.
I have counted all the sinners of the earth as lawbreakers. Therefore I have loved all your testimonies at all times.
Nail down my flesh through fear of you, for I have feared your judgments.
16 — Ayin. You have acted with justice and righteousness. Do not hand me over to those who oppress me.
Take your servant into your care for his good. Do not let the arrogant slander me.
My eyes have grown dim waiting for your salvation and for the word of your righteousness.
Deal with your servant according to your mercy, and teach me your statutes.
I am your servant. Teach me so that I may understand your testimonies.
It is time for the Lord to act. Teach me your law. They have broken your law.
For this reason I loved your commandments more than gold and topaz.
And so I walked uprightly in all your commandments; I hated every path of injustice.
17 — Pe. Your testimonies are wonderful; for this reason my soul searched them out.
The revelation of your words gives me light; your law teaches the little ones.
I opened my mouth and drew breath, longing for your commandments.
Look upon me and have mercy on me, according to your judgment for those who love your name.
Direct my steps according to your word, and do not let any lawlessness rule over me.
Rescue me from human slander, so that I may keep your commandments.
Reveal your face to your servant, and teach me your statutes.
My eyes poured out streams of water because they did not keep your law.
18 — Tsade. You are righteous, Lord, and your judgment is upright.
You commanded your testimonies in righteousness and great truth.
Zeal for your house consumed me because my enemies forgot your commandments.
Your word is thoroughly refined, and your servant keeps it.
I am small and despised, but I have not forgotten your statutes.
Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and your law is truth.
Trouble and distress came upon me; I will meditate on your commandments.
Your testimonies are righteousness forever. Teach me so that I may live.
19 — Qoph. I cried out with all my heart. Hear me, Lord; I will seek your statutes.
I cried out, saying, “Save me, so that I may keep your testimonies.”
I rose early and cried out because I put my trust in your words.
My eyes were awake before dawn to meditate on your words.
Hear my voice, Lord, according to your mercy; give me life according to your judgment.
Those who pursue me in lawlessness have drawn near, but they are far from your law.
You are near, Lord, and your commandments are true.
From the beginning I knew from your testimonies that you had established them forever.
20 — Resh. Look at my humiliation and rescue me, for I have not forgotten your law.
Judge my case and redeem me. Give me life according to your word.
Salvation is far from sinners, for they have not sought your statutes.
Your acts of compassion are very many, Lord. Give me life according to your word.
Many are those who pursue me and oppress me. I have not turned away from your testimonies.
I saw the foolish and fell apart, because they did not keep your words.
And because I have loved your commandments, give me life, Lord, in your mercy.
The beginning of your words is truth. All your righteous judgments endure forever.
21 — Shin. Rulers have pursued me without cause, and my heart shrank before your words.
I will rejoice over your word like someone who has found much plunder.
I hated injustice and rejected it, but I loved your law.
I praised you seven times a day for your righteous judgments.
Those who love your name have great peace, and there is no stumbling block for them.
I was waiting for your salvation, Lord, and I carried out your commandments.
My soul kept your testimonies, and I loved them greatly.
I kept your commandments and your judgments, for all my ways are before you, Lord.
22 — Taw. Let my plea draw near to you, Lord. Lord, teach me according to your word.
Let my honor come into your presence. Save me according to your word.
My lips will speak a blessing when you teach me your statutes.
My tongue will proclaim your words, for all your commandments are righteous.
Let your hand be there to save me, for I have desired your commandments.
I have loved your salvation, Lord, and your law is my meditation.
My soul will live and praise you, and your judgments will help me.
I have strayed like a lost sheep. Seek your servant and listen to me, for I have not forgotten your commandments.
A song of ascents. I cried out to you, Lord, when I was in distress, and you heard me.
Lord, rescue my soul from dishonest lips and from a deceitful tongue.
What will they give you, or what will they add to you, against a deceitful tongue?
The warrior’s sharpened arrows, together with burning coals from the desert.
Woe to me, because my dwelling place is far away! I have lived in the dwelling places of Kedar.
My soul has lived as a foreigner for a very long time.
I was peaceable among those who hate peace. Whenever I speak with them, they oppose me in battle.
A song of ascents. I lifted my eyes to the mountains. Where will my help come from?
My help comes from the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
Do not let my foot slip, and do not let the one who guards me fall asleep.
Look, the one who watches over Israel will neither doze nor sleep.
The Lord is the one who will guard you. The Lord is the shade over your right hand.
The sun will not scorch you by day, nor the moon by night.
The Lord will protect you from every evil; he will protect your soul.
He will protect your coming in and your going out forever and ever.
A song of ascents. I rejoiced over those who said to me, “We will go to the house of the Lord.”
Our feet were standing in your courts, Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is built like a city whose parts are joined together.
For the tribes went up there, the tribes of the Lord, as a testimony for Israel, to acknowledge your name, Lord.
For thrones were set there for judgment, thrones for the house of David.
Seek the things that bring peace to Jerusalem, and prosperity for those who love you.
May there be peace within your strength and prosperity within your palaces.
For the sake of my brothers and those close to me, I spoke of peace for you.
For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I sought good things.
A song of ascents. I lifted my eyes to you, Lord, who dwell in heaven.
As the eyes of servants look to the hands of their masters, and as the eyes of a maidservant look to the hand of her mistress, so your eyes look to the Lord our God until he has compassion on us.
Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, for we have been filled with contempt beyond measure.
For our soul has been filled beyond measure [?] the mockery of those who ridicule and the contempt of the proud.
A song of upheavals. If the Lord had not been on our side—let Israel say—
if the Lord had not been on our side when people rose up against us,
they would have swallowed us alive when their anger flared up against us.
They would have swallowed us alive; the water would have drowned us.
Our soul passed through a torrent; our soul was passing through the raging water.
Blessed is the Lord, who did not give us as food for their teeth.
Our soul escaped like a bird from the hunters’ trap. The trap broke, and we escaped.
Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.
The song of ascents. Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion. The one who dwells in Jerusalem will never be shaken.
The mountains surround her, and the Lord surrounds his people, from now on and forever.
For he will not leave the rod of sinners over the allotted land of the righteous, so that the righteous will not stretch out their hands to commit lawless deeds.
Lord, do good to those who are good and to those who are upright in their hearts.
But those who turn aside into crooked ways, the Lord will cast out along with those who commit lawlessness. Peace be upon Israel.
Song of ascents. When the Lord brought back his people from captivity, we became like those who had been comforted.
Then our mouth was filled with joy, and our tongue with rejoicing. Then they will say among the nations, “The Lord has done great things for these people.”
The Lord has done great things for us, and we became glad.
Lord, restore us from captivity like a torrent in the south.
Those who sow in tears will reap with joy. They went along weeping, carrying their seeds.
But when they come, they come with rejoicing, carrying their sheaves.
A song of upheavals. Of Solomon. Unless the Lord builds a house, those who build it have labored in vain. Unless the Lord guards a city, its guard has spent a sleepless night in vain.
It is useless for you to rise early after sitting down, you who eat the bread of sorrow, when he gives sleep to his beloved.
Look, children are the Lord’s inheritance; look, the fruit of the womb is a reward.
Like arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of those who have been cast out.
Blessed is the man who will fulfill his desire with them. They will not be put to shame when they speak with their enemies at the gates.
A song of upheavals. Blessed are all who fear the Lord, who walk in his ways.
You will eat the fruits of your labor. You are blessed, and things will go well for you.
Your wife will be like flourishing grapevines in the inner rooms of your house; your children will be like newly planted olive trees around your table.
Look, this is how the person who fears the Lord will be blessed.
May the Lord bless you from Zion, and may you see the good things of Jerusalem all the days of your life.
And may you see your children's children. Peace be upon Israel.
A song of ascents. They have fought against me many times since my youth.
Let Israel say, "They have fought against me many times in my youth, but they have not overcome me."
Sinners plotted against me behind my back; they made the path of their lawlessness long.
The Lord is righteous; he cut the necks of sinners.
Let everyone who hates Zion be put to shame and turn back.
Let them be like grass on the rooftops, which dries up before it is pulled out.
It does not fill the reaper's hand, nor does the one gathering its sheaves fill his lap.
Those passing by did not say, “The Lord’s blessing be upon you. We bless you in the name of the Lord.”
A song of ascents. From the depths I cried out to you, Lord. Lord, hear my voice.
Let your ears pay attention to the sound of my plea.
Lord, if you keep account of lawlessness, who will be able to stand?
For forgiveness is with you. For the sake of your name, I waited for you, Lord.
My soul waited for your word.
My soul hoped in the Lord from morning until evening. Let Israel hope in the Lord from the morning watch.
For mercy is with the Lord, and abundant redemption is with him.
And he is the one who will redeem Israel from all its lawlessness.
A song of ascents. Lord, my heart was not proud, nor were my eyes haughty. I did not pursue great things or wonders beyond me.
If I did not humble myself, but exalted my soul, then, like a child weaned from its mother, such is the repayment for my soul.
Let Israel hope in the Lord from now on and forever.
A song of ascents. Lord, remember David and all his gentleness.
Remember how he swore to the Lord and made a vow to the God of Jacob:
"I will not enter the dwelling of my house or climb onto the bedding of my bed.
I will not give sleep to my eyes, slumber to my eyelids, or rest to my temples,
until I find a place for the Lord, a dwelling for the God of Jacob."
Look, we heard of it in Ephrathah; we found it in the field of the woods.
We will enter his dwelling place and worship in the place where his feet stood.
Rise, Lord, and go to your resting place, you and your holy ark.
Your priests will clothe themselves in righteousness, and your holy ones will rejoice.
For the sake of David your servant, do not turn your face away from your anointed one.
The Lord swore to David in truth, and he will not break his promise: “I will seat one of your descendants on your throne.
If your sons keep my covenant and my testimonies, which I will teach them, their sons too will sit on your throne forever.”
For the Lord chose Zion; he desired it as his dwelling place.
“This is my dwelling place forever and ever. I will live here, because I desired it.
I will richly bless its widow; I will satisfy its poor with bread.
I will clothe its priests with salvation, and its holy ones will rejoice greatly.”
There I will make a horn sprout for David. I have prepared a lamp for my anointed one.
I will clothe his enemies in shame, but my holiness will blossom upon him.
A song of ascents. Look, what is good or pleasant other than brothers living together in one place?
They will be like the oil on Aaron’s head, running down onto his beard, running down onto the edges of his garments.
They will be like the dew of Hermon that comes down upon the mountains of Zion, for there the Lord commanded his blessing: life forever.
A song of ascents. Bless the Lord, all you servants of the Lord who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courtyards of the house of our God.
Lift your hands toward the holy place at night, and bless the Lord.
May the Lord, who made heaven and earth, bless you from Zion.
Hallelujah. Bless the name of the Lord. Servants, bless the Lord,
you who stand in the Lord’s house, in the courtyards of the house of our God.
Bless the Lord, for the Lord is good. Sing praises to his name, for it is pleasant.
For the Lord chose Jacob for himself, Israel as his own possession.
For I know that the Lord is great, and that our Lord is above all gods.
Everything the Lord desired, they did in heaven and on earth,
in the seas and the depths. He brought clouds up from the ends of the earth; he made lightning for the rain. He brought winds out of their storehouses.
He struck every firstborn in Egypt, from humans to livestock.
He sent signs and wonders into your midst, Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his servants.
He [?] many nations and killed mighty kings:
Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan, and all the kings of Canaan.
He gave their land as an inheritance to Israel, his people.
Lord, your name lasts forever; your remembrance, Lord, lasts from generation to generation.
For the Lord will judge his people, and he will be comforted concerning his servants.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
They have eyes but do not see; they have ears but do not hear.

They have mouths but do not speak; they have noses but do not smell. They have hands but cannot act; they have feet but do not walk. They make no sound in their throats, for there is no breath in their mouths.
Those who made them will become like them, along with everyone who trusts in them.
House of Israel, bless the Lord! House of Levi, bless the Lord!
House of Aaron, bless the Lord! You who fear the Lord, bless the Lord!
Blessed is the Lord in Zion, he who dwells in Jerusalem.
Alleluia, doubled. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy lasts forever.
Give thanks to the God of gods, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who alone made wonders, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who made the heavens with wisdom, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who laid the earth's foundations upon the water, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who made the great lights, for his mercy lasts forever.
The sun to rule the day, for his mercy lasts forever.
The moon and the stars to rule the night, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who struck Egypt and its firstborn, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who [?] Israel out from among them, for his mercy lasts forever.
With a strong hand and a raised arm, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who divided the Red Sea into parts, for his mercy lasts forever.
He [?] Israel out from her midst, for his mercy lasts forever.
He cast Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who [?] his people out in the wilderness, for his mercy lasts forever. He who brought water out of a hard rock, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who struck the great kings, for his mercy lasts forever.
He killed mighty kings, for his mercy lasts forever.
Sihon, king of the Amorites, for his mercy lasts forever.
Og, the king of Bashan, for his mercy lasts forever.
He gave their land as an inheritance, for his mercy lasts forever.
As an inheritance to Israel his servant, for his mercy lasts forever.
The Lord remembered us in our humiliation, for his mercy lasts forever.
He rescued us from our enemies, for his mercy lasts forever.
He who gives food to all flesh, for his mercy lasts forever. Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his mercy lasts forever.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his mercy lasts forever.
Of Jeremiah. There by the rivers of Babylon we sat down and wept as we remembered Zion.
We hung our instruments on the willow branches in its midst.
For there those who took us captive asked for the words of a song, and those who seized us said, “Sing us a song of praise. Sing one of the songs of Zion.”
How can we sing the Lord’s song in a foreign land?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand be forgotten. May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth.
If I do not remember you, if I do not place Jerusalem above my greatest joy.
Remember, Lord, the children of Edom and the glory of Jerusalem, those who said, “Destroy it! Destroy it down to its foundations!”
Wretched daughter of Babylon, happy is the one who repays you for what you did to us.
Happy is the one who seizes your children and dashes them against the rock.
Of Zechariah. For David. I will give thanks to you, Lord, with all my heart, because you have heard the words of my mouth, and I will sing praises to you before the angels.
I will worship before your holy temple. I will give thanks to your name for your mercy and your truth, because you have exalted your holy name above everyone.
On the day when I cry out to you, hurry and hear me. You will strengthen me in my soul with great power.
Let all the kings of the earth give thanks to you, Lord, because they have heard the words of my mouth.
And let them sing the songs of the Lord, because the Lord’s glory is great.
For the Lord is exalted, and he looks upon the lowly, and he sees the exalted from far away.
If I walk into the midst of distress, you will keep me alive. You stretched out your hand against the anger of your enemies, and your right hand kept me alive.
The Lord will act on my behalf. Lord, your mercy lasts forever. Do not abandon the works of your hands.
For the end. A psalm of David. Of Zechariah, in the dispersion. Lord, you have examined me and known me.
You have known my sitting down and my rising up. You have understood all my thoughts from far away.
You have searched my path and my measuring line, and you have seen all my ways.
For there is no deceit on my tongue. Look, Lord, you know what is to come and what came before.
You formed me and laid your hand on me.
Your knowledge has become wonderful within me; it has grown mighty, and I cannot attain it.
Where will I go away from your Spirit? Or where will I flee from your presence?
If I go up to heaven, you are there. If I go down to the underworld, you are with me.
If I take my wings at dawn and settle at the farthest reaches of the sea, even there your hand,
your right hand will lead me and hold me.
Then I said, “Darkness will overwhelm me,” and the night became light in my delight.
For no darkness will hide anything from you, and the night will shine like the day. Its darkness is just like its light.
For you, Lord, acquired my kidneys for yourself, and you took me to yourself from within my mother.
I will praise you, for I have been greatly astonished. Your works are wonders, and my soul knows them very well.
In secret, my bones were not hidden from you, which you made in secret, and my strength in the depths of the earth.
Your eyes saw my unformed body. They will all be written in your book; they will fill the day, and you will grow among them.
Your friends, O God, have become very great in my eyes; their authority has become very powerful.
I will count them, and they will be more numerous than the sand. I awoke, and I am still with you.
God, if you kill sinners—bloodthirsty men, get away from me!
For God will speak while they plot; they will take your cities in vain.
Lord, I hated those who hate you, and I wasted away because of your enemies.
I hated them with a great hatred; they became my enemies.
Test me, God, and know my heart. Examine me and know my ways.
See whether there is a lawless way within me, and lead me along an everlasting way.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Lord, save me from an evil person; rescue me from a violent person.
These are the ones who devised evil things in their hearts; they stirred up wars all day long.
They sharpened their tongues like snakes; snake venom is under their lips. Pause.
Protect me, Lord, from the sinner’s hand. Save me from violent men, who planned to make my steps stumble.
The proud hid a trap for me. They stretched out ropes as a snare for my feet. They set stumbling blocks for me close to my path. Pause.
I said to the Lord, “You are my God. Lord, listen to the sound of my plea.”
Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation, you sheltered me on the day of battle.
Lord, do not hand me over, in my desire, to a sinner. They have plotted against me. Do not abandon me, lest they become proud. Pause.
As for the head of their gathering, the trouble caused by their lips will surround them.
Coals will fall on them, and you will cast them into fire. They will not be able to stand amid their miseries.
A slanderer will not prosper on the earth. Evil will hunt down a violent man to destroy him.
I know that the Lord will uphold the cause of the poor and secure justice for the needy.
But the righteous will give thanks to your name; the upright will dwell in your presence.
A psalm of David. I cried out to you, Lord. Listen to me; pay attention to my voice when I cry out to you.
Let my prayer rise like incense before you, and the lifting of my hands like an evening sacrifice.
Lord, you have placed a guard at my mouth and a secure door at my lips.
Do not turn my heart toward evil words, so that I make excuses for sins with people who practice lawlessness. I will not take counsel with their chosen ones.
The righteous person will discipline me with mercy and rebuke me. But do not let the sinner’s oil anoint my head. Still, still, my prayer is in their desire.
The mighty ones of the earth were swallowed up beside the rock. Listen to my words, for they have become powerful. Like a clod of earth, they were split apart on the ground.
Our bones were scattered at the mouth of the underworld.
For my eyes are lifted toward you, Lord. I have placed my hope in you; do not take away my life.
Guard me from the trap they have set for me, and from the snares of those who practice lawlessness.
The sinner will fall into his own net. I am alone until I pass him by.
An instruction of David. A prayer when he was in the cave.
With my voice I cried out to the Lord; with my voice I pleaded with the Lord.
I will pour out my prayer before him; I will tell him of my distress.
When my spirit grew faint within me, you knew my paths. They hid a trap for me on the path where I walked.
I looked to my right and saw that no one knew me. I found no way to escape, and no one cares for my soul.
I cried out to you, Lord. I said, “You are my hope, my portion in the land of the living.”
Pay attention to the sound of my pleading, for I have been brought very low. Rescue me from those pursuing me, for they have become stronger than I am.
Bring my soul out of prison so that I may proclaim your name, Lord. The righteous are waiting for me until you repay me.
A psalm of David, when his son pursued him. Lord, listen to my prayer; hear my plea in your truth. Listen to me in your righteousness.
Do not enter into judgment with your servant, for no person will be declared righteous before you.
For the enemy pursued my soul; he crushed my life down to the ground. He humbled me in dark places, like those who have been dead forever.
And my spirit was grieved; my heart was troubled within me.
I remembered the days of old. I meditated on all your deeds; I meditated on the works of your hands.
I stretched out my hands toward you. My soul became like thirsty ground before you. Musical interlude.
Hear me quickly, Lord, for my spirit has grown faint. Do not turn your face away from me, lest I become like those who go down into the pit.
Let me hear of your mercy in the morning, for I have placed my hope in you. Show me, Lord, the way I should go, for I have lifted up my soul to you.
Save me from my enemies, Lord, for I have fled to you.
Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your good spirit will lead me along a straight path.
You will give me life for the sake of your name, Lord. In your righteousness, you will [?] my soul out of distress.
In your mercy, you will wipe out my enemies. You will destroy everyone who afflicts my soul, for I am your servant.
Of David, against Goliath. Blessed is the Lord my God, who trains my hands for battle and my fingers for war.
My mercy and my refuge, the one who shelters me and my deliverer, my stronghold in whom I have trusted, the one who subjects the people to me.
Lord, what is a human being that you have revealed yourself to him, or a son of man that you take account of him?
A human being is like something without substance; his days are like shadows.
Lord, bend down the heavens and come down. Touch the mountains, and let them give off smoke.
Flash lightning and scatter them. Shoot your arrows and throw them into confusion.
Send out your hand from on high. Save me and rescue me from the many waters and from the hand of foreigners.
Their mouth has spoken worthless things, and their right hand is a right hand of wrongdoing.
God, I will sing a new song to you. I will sing praises to you on a ten-stringed harp.
The one who gives victory to kings, the one who rescues David his servant from an evil sword.
Rescue me and save me from a foreigner. Their mouth has spoken what is worthless; their right hand is a [?] of wrongdoing.
These are the ones whose sons are like young plants planted in their youth. Their daughters are adorned, fashioned like temples.
Their storerooms are full, overflowing from one to another. Their sheep bear many young and multiply in their outlying places.
Their cattle are fat. There is no collapse of walls or route for going in and out, nor is there an outcry in their squares.
They called the people who have these things blessed. Blessed are the people whose God is the Lord.
David’s praise. I will exalt you, my God, my king. I will bless your name forever and forevermore.
I will bless you every day, and I will bless your name forever and forevermore.
The Lord is great and greatly blessed, and his greatness has no measure.
One generation after another will praise your deeds and proclaim your power.
And they will tell of the glorious splendor of your greatness; they will speak of your wonders.
And they will proclaim the power of your fearsome deeds; they will speak of your greatness.
Let them proclaim the memory of your abundant goodness and rejoice in your righteousness.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful; he is patient, and his mercy is great.
The Lord is good in everything, and his compassion rests on all his works.
Let all your works acknowledge you, Lord, and let your holy ones bless you.
They will tell of the glory of your kingdom; they will speak of the glory of your power,
to make your power known to humanity, and the glory of the greatness of your kingdom.
Your kingdom is a kingdom that lasts forever, and your rule lasts through every generation. The Lord is faithful in his words, and he is holy in all his works.
The Lord supports everyone who is falling, and he raises to their feet all who have been cast down.
Everyone's eyes look expectantly to you, and you will give them food at the proper time.
You will open your hand and satisfy everyone according to your will.
The Lord is righteous in all his ways, and he is holy in all his works.
The Lord is near to everyone who calls out to him, everyone who calls out to him in truth.
He will fulfill the desire of everyone who fears him, and he will hear their plea and save them.
The Lord will protect everyone who loves him, and he will wipe out all sinners.
My mouth will speak the praise of the Lord. Let all flesh bless his holy name forever and forever and ever.
Alleluia. Of Haggai and Zechariah. My soul, bless the Lord.
I will bless the Lord throughout my life; I will sing praises to my God as long as I exist.
Do not trust in rulers or in human beings, who have no power to save.
Their spirit leaves them, and they return to their earth. On that day all their thoughts will perish.
Blessed is the one whose helper is the God of Jacob, and whose hope rests on the Lord his God,
who made heaven and earth, the sea and everything in it, who preserves his truth forever,
who gives justice to those who are oppressed, who gives food to the hungry. The Lord will release those who are bound.
The Lord will raise up those who have fallen. The Lord will instruct the blind. The Lord is with the righteous.
The Lord protects foreigners. He will take the orphan and the widow into his care, and he will destroy the way of sinners.
The Lord will reign forever, your God, Zion, from generation to generation.
Hallelujah! Praise the Lord, for a psalm is good; praise is pleasing to our God.
The Lord builds Jerusalem; he gathers together the scattered people of Israel.
He heals those whose hearts are broken and binds up their wounds.
He counts the multitude of stars and gives names to them all.
Our Lord is great, and his power is great; his understanding has no limit.
The Lord lifts up the humble and brings sinners down to the ground.
Begin with thanksgiving to the Lord; sing to our God with a harp.
He covered the sky with clouds and prepared rain for the earth; he makes grass grow on the mountains.
Who gives food to their livestock and to the young ravens that cry out to him.
He does not delight in the strength of a horse, nor does he take pleasure in a man's thighs.
The Lord takes pleasure in those who fear him and those who hope in his mercy.
Hallelujah! Of Haggai and Zechariah. Jerusalem, honor the Lord! Zion, praise your God!
For he strengthened the bars of your gates and blessed your children within you.
He made your borders peaceful and satisfied you with the finest wheat.
He sends his word to the earth; his word will run swiftly.
He gives snow like wool and scatters frost like ashes.
He throws down ice like morsels. Who can stand before his cold?
His wind will blow, and the waters will flow.
He declares his word to Jacob, his statutes and his judgments to Israel.
He has not done this for any other nation, nor has he made his judgments known to them.
Hallelujah! Of Haggai and Zechariah. Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him from the heights!
Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his powers!
Praise him, sun and moon! All the stars and the light, praise him!
Heavens of heavens, praise him! Let the waters above the heavens praise the name of the Lord.
For he spoke, and they came into being; he commanded, and they were created.
He established them forever and for all eternity. He gave them a decree that they will not transgress.
Praise the Lord from the earth, you dragons and all the depths.
Fire, hail, snow, and ice, storm winds that carry out his word;
Mountains and all hills, fruit-bearing trees and cedars;
Wild animals and all livestock, creeping creatures and birds;
Kings and the earth, and every people, rulers and all the judges of the earth;
Young men and young women, old people and children.
Let them all praise the name of the Lord, because his name alone is exalted, and his manifestation is above the earth and heaven.
He will raise the horn of his people. This is the praise of all his holy ones, the children of Israel, the people who are close to him.
Hallelujah. Sing to the Lord a new song; sing his praise in the assembly of the holy ones.
Let Israel rejoice in the one who made him. Let the children of Zion rejoice in their king.
Let them praise the name of the Lord with dancing; let them sing to him with a tambourine and a harp.
For the Lord takes pleasure in his people, and he will exalt the gentle with salvation.
The holy ones will boast in glory, and they will rejoice on their beds.
The exaltation of God is in their throats, and double-edged swords are in their hands,
To take vengeance on the nations and punish the peoples,
To bind kings with chains and their honored men with bronze shackles,
To carry out against them a written judgment. This is the glory of all his holy ones.
Hallelujah. Praise the Lord among his holy ones. Praise him in the firmament of his power.
Praise him for his mighty deeds. Praise him for his abundant greatness.
Praise him with the sound of a trumpet; praise him with a harp and a lyre.
Praise him with tambourine and dancing. Praise the Lord with strings and musical instruments.
Praise him with sweet-sounding cymbals. Praise him with cymbals of rejoicing.
Let everything that breathes praise the Lord.

The Psalms of David. This psalm, which David wrote for himself, is outside the numbering, when he fought Goliath. I was small among my brothers, insignificant in my father's house, tending my father's sheep.
My hands made a musical instrument; my fingers tuned a harp.
Who will report to the Lord? He is the Lord; he is the one who hears.
He is the one who sent his angel, took me from my father’s sheep, and anointed me with the oil of his anointing.
My brothers were tall and handsome, but the Lord did not want them.
I went out to meet the Philistine, and he cursed me by his idols.
But I drew his sword from his hand, cut off his head, and removed disgrace from the children of Israel. The Book of Psalms.
